short.en: the readiness not to insist on everything in a conflict but to find a solution that suits everyone

def.en: Her willingness to compromise seemed so natural, as if she had never learned to insist on her own position.

short.en: the inner drive that makes one do something or keep going

def.en: The motivation in the team rose so strongly, as if all employees had received a personal pay rise.

short.en: to say what one thinks or how one judges something

def.en: In the meeting she clearly and objectively expressed her opinion; afterwards the team's position was definitively established.

short.en: a phrase used to introduce one's own view

def.en: In my opinion the decision has not yet been definitively made; the minutes must first be approved by management.

term.en: i am of the opinion that …

short.en: a more formal phrase used to express one's own conviction

def.en: I am of the opinion that the new regulation has not yet been sufficiently communicated and should first be explained to all employees.

short.en: a phrase used to express one's assessment of something

def.en: I consider it sensible that the workshop results are recorded in writing before the next meeting begins.

short.en: to have the same opinion as someone else and to express this

def.en: All team members agreed to the proposal; with that the decision was officially made.

short.en: to have a different opinion from someone else and to say so directly

def.en: He disagreed with the proposal objectively, even though the direction had already been decided by the majority.

short.en: to not accept an idea, a proposal or a request

def.en: The proposal was clearly rejected by a majority in the vote; the decision is thus definitively made.

short.en: to agree with a decision or proposal

def.en: All parties involved were in agreement; the arrangement is therefore officially confirmed.

short.en: to disapprove of an idea or decision and to say so

def.en: He was against it from the start; his objection is clearly noted in the minutes.

short.en: to approve of and support an idea or decision

def.en: The majority was in favour; therefore the new proposal is officially accepted with immediate effect.

term.en: to hold a position, to advocate a view

short.en: to hold a particular opinion and advocate it publicly

def.en: She held the position that the project had to be extended; this stance is documented in the meeting minutes.

short.en: argued or presented so well that others are persuaded

def.en: His presentation was so convincing that the budget request is immediately approved.

short.en: to present reasons in such a way that others can follow and share one's opinion

def.en: Whoever argues convincingly ensures that their position is clearly understood before the vote takes place.

short.en: a reason or justification used to support an opinion

def.en: The strongest argument for the new strategy is clearly worked out in the presentation.

short.en: a reason that speaks against an opinion or a proposal

def.en: The decisive counter-argument has not been refuted by either side in the debate.

short.en: a conversation in which different opinions are exchanged and evaluated

def.en: The discussion about the new working hours is finally concluded after three hours of debate.

short.en: to talk about a topic on which there are different opinions

def.en: After the team discussed for hours, a common compromise has been found.

short.en: a structured, public discussion on a controversial topic

def.en: The debate on the new home-office model has not yet been officially concluded; a resolution is still pending.

short.en: to abandon one's own resistance and agree with someone else's view

def.en: He finally gave in; with that the point of contention is formally settled.

short.en: to do something in a way that avoids unnecessary risk

def.en: In order to play it safe, the agreement was put in writing; everything is thus legally secured.

short.en: to stick to one's opinion or demand even when others are against it

def.en: He insisted on his position; it is now officially recorded in the minutes and must be discussed again at the next meeting.

short.en: a result in which all parties have agreed on a common solution

def.en: After lengthy negotiations an agreement has finally been reached; both parties can accept the compromise.

short.en: to be successful with one's own opinion or demand even though others were against it

def.en: She prevailed; her approach is now established as the official procedure.

short.en: the arguments that speak for and against a decision

def.en: The pros and cons are listed in detail in the report; the team can now make a well-founded decision.

short.en: to carefully compare different options or arguments before deciding

def.en: All options <g>have been</g> carefully <g>weighed up</g> by the team; now the decision can be made.

short.en: the result drawn from facts or a discussion

def.en: The most important conclusion of the report is clearly formulated and will be presented to the board tomorrow.

short.en: structured in a way that everything fits together sensibly and contains no contradictions

def.en: The argumentation is completely coherent; all points are logically aligned with one another.

short.en: in a way that one can believe and follow

def.en: His explanation sounds completely plausible; the connection is clearly presented to everyone.

short.en: the way in which someone leads and structures a conversation or discussion

def.en: The facilitation is clearly regulated: the moderator gives the floor and ensures a factual atmosphere.

short.en: the opinion or stance that someone holds on a topic

def.en: The union's position has already been formulated in an official statement and forwarded to the press.

short.en: the right to express one's own opinion freely without being punished for it

def.en: Freedom of opinion is enshrined in the German constitution as a fundamental right and also applies in labour law.

short.en: achieving more together

def.en: By working more closely together, the departments create a synergy that strengthens the entire company.

short.en: to make a contribution to a result or success

def.en: By every team member bringing in their strengths, each can actively contribute to the project's success.

short.en: one's own share in the result

def.en: By everyone making their contribution, the shared goal is reached faster and more efficiently.

short.en: someone one can depend on

def.en: By always delivering reliably, the department has earned an excellent reputation in the company.

short.en: an agreement made in advance

def.en: By making a clear prior agreement, misunderstandings were avoided from the outset.

short.en: to agree on something together

def.en: By the procedure being carefully agreed on in advance, the meeting ran more efficiently than expected.

short.en: the passing on of tasks to others

def.en: By consistently practising delegation, the manager creates space for strategic decisions.

short.en: the participation of other people

def.en: By the inclusion of all team members being ensured, decisions are better accepted.

short.en: to inform openly and clearly

def.en: By management communicating transparently, trust is built and rumours are prevented.

short.en: a goal that all share

def.en: By the team having a clear shared goal, everyone's efforts are aligned.

term.en: to agree, to be in agreement

short.en: to be of the same opinion

def.en: By the positions of both sides agreeing, a joint resolution can be made more quickly.

short.en: to make contact with someone

def.en: By them getting in touch with the customer in good time, problems are clarified early.

short.en: to consider something

def.en: By the needs of all involved being taken into account, the solution is accepted more broadly.

short.en: to coordinate something together with others

def.en: By both departments regularly coordinating with each other, redundancies are avoided.

term.en: to remind, to follow up on

short.en: to remind someone again or demand something again

def.en: By the team leader following up on outstanding reports, delays are prevented.

short.en: to find a common agreement together

def.en: By both parties being willing to reach an understanding, the conflict is resolved more quickly.

short.en: before something happens

def.en: By all documents being distributed in advance, the meeting can be conducted more efficiently.

short.en: fitting to something, in line with it

def.en: By all employees being trained accordingly, quality is noticeably improved.

short.en: a meeting within the team

def.en: By regular team meetings taking place, everyone stays informed and tasks are clearly distributed.

short.en: to make something available for others

def.en: By all relevant documents being made digitally accessible, everyone is kept up to date.

short.en: people or companies that compete with each other

def.en: By the team analysing the competitors carefully, its own strengths can be used more effectively.

short.en: a negative reaction to another's success

def.en: By managers speaking openly about successes, envy in the team is reduced.

short.en: hostile behaviour

def.en: By conflicts being addressed early, aggression in the team is prevented.

short.en: to shame someone in front of others

def.en: By nobody in the team being embarrassed publicly, the working atmosphere is improved.

short.en: not enough, deficient

def.en: By insufficient performance being addressed early, improvement can be achieved.

short.en: to accept an apology

def.en: By the manager being willing to accept an apology, the conflict is resolved and trust is restored.

short.en: to speak privately and confidentially

def.en: By sensitive topics being discussed in private, dignity is preserved and solutions are found more easily.

short.en: to stick to one's opinion

def.en: By her insisting on her position without listening, a compromise cannot be found.

term.en: to be able to understand, to comprehend

short.en: to understand something logically

def.en: By the manager explaining her decisions, they can be better understood by the team.

short.en: a special occasion or event

def.en: By the company organising an annual event, team cohesion is strengthened.

short.en: measures to strengthen the team and its cohesion

def.en: By the company regularly investing in team building, trust among colleagues is continuously built up.

short.en: probably, as expected

def.en: By the project presumably being completed in June, planning can begin now.

short.en: humorous and amusing

def.en: By the team leader being funny and approachable, the working atmosphere is experienced as more pleasant.

short.en: products shown in a shop window to attract customers

def.en: The window display was designed both creatively and clearly to attract customers.

term.en: co-design / active participation in shaping something

short.en: actively taking part in planning or changing something together with others

def.en: The opportunity to participate in shaping the new work concept was possible not only for management, but also for all employees.

short.en: a short title above a text or section; shows what it is about

def.en: The heading of the cover letter should be formulated both clearly and professionally.

short.en: well-ordered and easy to understand; easy to navigate

def.en: A CV should be not only clearly structured, but also visually appealing, so the employer can quickly find the key information.

term.en: to find one's way / to get the hang of something

short.en: to know where one is or how something works; to cope well with a situation

def.en: On his first day at work, he quickly found his way around both the new company and the new team.

term.en: to list / to cite / to present

short.en: to show, present or enumerate something

def.en: In a CV one should list both activities and qualifications completely.

short.en: things are connected or dependent; one understands how they fit together

def.en: There is a clear connection between good education and career opportunities. In a CV, the professional context must be presented clearly, either chronologically or thematically.

short.en: the opportunity to see or understand something; a first impression

def.en: The internship not only gives a good insight into the profession, but also helps in deciding on a training programme.

short.en: using imagination and one's own ideas to create or design something

def.en: Creative design is an important skill both in graphic design and in architecture.

term.en: to state / to indicate / to specify

short.en: to name or communicate something; to provide information in writing or verbally

def.en: In the application form you must state both your school leaving qualification and professional experience.

short.en: to not do something or to go around it in order to prevent problems

def.en: In a CV one should either avoid gaps or explain them clearly.

term.en: to enclose / to attach / to add

short.en: to add something to something else; e.g. documents to an application

def.en: Please enclose both a recent photo and all relevant certificates with your application.

term.en: the technical secondary school / vocational technical school

short.en: school after primary school providing technical and vocational education

def.en: After secondary school he attended a technical school that offered both practical and theoretical training, and became an electrician.

short.en: school-leaving qualification entitling one to study at a university; in germany = abitur

def.en: With a university entrance qualification one can study either at a university or at a university of applied sciences in Germany.

term.en: the professional career path / work history

short.en: all stages of education, work and professional activity; important for CV and job applications

def.en: In my professional career I worked as a nursing specialist in a hospital. Please attach your professional career history to your CV, either in tabular form or as continuous text.

term.en: the freight forwarding company / logistics company

short.en: company that organises freight transport by road, rail, sea or air, including customs and storage

def.en: The freight forwarding company organises both the transport and the storage of goods from the manufacturer to the customer.

term.en: to handle / to process / to carry out

short.en: to complete a task or carry out a process from start to finish

def.en: The freight company handles all transport orders both quickly and reliably.

term.en: to redesign / to restructure / to transform

short.en: to change, renew or redesign something

def.en: The company has redesigned its application process to be not only more digital, but also faster.

short.en: creates scale drawings, floor plans and detail drawings for buildings, bridges or roads

def.en: Both the draughtsperson and the architect are involved in the creation of a building: the former creates the technical construction drawings, the latter plans and designs.

short.en: technical drawing of a building from a specific side: front, side or top view

def.en: The draughtsperson created both the elevations and the sections of the building.

short.en: recruitment consultant for top specialists

def.en: A headhunter not only searches for suitable candidates, but also carefully analyses their career potential.

short.en: person entrusted with specific tasks

def.en: The company's data protection officer is responsible both for compliance with all data protection laws and for training employees.

short.en: to attract someone for a position

def.en: The company wants to recruit new talent – admittedly the market is tight, but attractive offers make it possible.

short.en: in reality, normally or originally

def.en: I actually wanted to become an architect, but then I decided on technical draughting.

short.en: but, however; introduces a limitation or contrast

def.en: The new job is very interesting; however, the working hours are sometimes very long.

short.en: work shift during the night

def.en: Both hospitals and manufacturing companies pay allowances for the night shift in order to attract staff.

short.en: fortbildung = current profession; weiterbildung = new skills for a different role

def.en: Both the doctor doing professional development on new treatment methods and the shop assistant doing further training to become a manager are investing in their future.

short.en: business entity

def.en: Both the company and the individual employees benefit from a clear training structure.

short.en: in each case

def.en: We meet respectively on Mondays for the team meeting; in doing so, we plan the coming week together.

short.en: necessary condition

def.en: Both good German skills and a recognised school certificate are important prerequisites for studying.

short.en: in place of

def.en: She opted for a dual study programme <g>instead of</g> directly <g>starting</g> a classic apprenticeship.

short.en: tiring / difficult

def.en: The path to graduation was admittedly very arduous, but in the end the effort paid off.

short.en: alternative explanation

def.en: In a cover letter one should use neither jargon nor an overly complicated paraphrase of one's tasks.

short.en: to do in turns

def.en: <g>The more often</g> theory and practice <g>alternate</g> in dual training, <g>the better</g> the knowledge is consolidated.

short.en: large event for product presentation

def.en: At the trade fair one can either talk to HR representatives or simply gather information about open positions.

short.en: plan or intent

def.en: She expressed not only the intention to go abroad but also a concrete plan for it.

short.en: limit / reduction

def.en: The position sounds interesting; however, there is a restriction regarding working hours.

short.en: option / choice

def.en: Both a degree programme and a dual apprenticeship are sensible alternatives after graduating from school.

short.en: contradiction

def.en: His CV did admittedly seem convincing, but a clear contrast to his statements emerged in the interview.

short.en: hotel management pro

def.en: As a hotel management specialist, one takes on both organisational tasks and staff management.

short.en: happening

def.en: The more significant an event in the CV is, the more detailed the description should be.

short.en: facility management

def.en: The janitorial service takes care of neither only repairs nor exclusively garden maintenance, but of both.

short.en: positive outlook

def.en: She actually had little confidence, but the interview went surprisingly well.

short.en: issuing an invoice

def.en: The new software not only speeds up invoicing considerably, but also reduces the error rate.

short.en: understanding

def.en: However, the realization that a career change was necessary only came after several unsuccessful applications.

short.en: in any case

def.en: He wanted to quit anyway – admittedly he had no new position yet, but the decision was firm.

short.en: long-term impact

def.en: Both a good working atmosphere and fair pay contribute to sustainable employee retention.

short.en: hours beyond normal time

def.en: Either overtime is financially compensated, or it is balanced with time off.

short.en: working on official public holidays

def.en: Work on public holidays is neither mandatory for all sectors nor always voluntary – the law precisely regulates the allowances.

short.en: salary, wages, fees

def.en: He asked directly during the interview in order to gain clarity about the remuneration.

short.en: sick leave reporting

def.en: Anyone who cannot work due to illness needs a certificate of incapacity for work in order to continue receiving wages.

short.en: protection of internal info

def.en: The confidentiality obligation prohibits employees from disclosing internal company data without first informing management.

short.en: time off instead of pay

def.en: For performed overtime, the employer can pay extra wages or grant compensatory time off in order to balance the workload of the employees.

short.en: self-marketing

def.en: In the cover letter, the motto is: promote yourself instead of just listing dry facts, and convince the boss of your strengths!

short.en: e-mail element

def.en: In the subject line of an application e-mail, it is best to write the exact job title in order to immediately attract attention.

short.en: commencement of work

def.en: The employer asked me during the interview about my earliest possible starting date in order to finalize personnel planning.

short.en: information / help

def.en: The Federal Employment Agency offers a free consultation for career orientation in order to help job seekers.

short.en: carrying out a process or transaction

def.en: The project manager defined clear responsibilities in order to ensure smooth processing of all tasks.

short.en: to extract information

def.en: You can gather further details about the salary from the attached employment contract without needing to ask the HR office separately.

short.en: clear and informative

def.en: A successful application needs meaningful documents in order to show your skills immediately.

short.en: in great detail

def.en: During the interview, the department manager explained the tasks in great detail in order to avoid misunderstandings from the start.

short.en: occurring during work

def.en: The janitor takes care of all repairs arising in and around the building without hesitating for long.

short.en: expert knowledge

def.en: Customers highly appreciate his expert advice on technical problems instead of researching for a long time themselves.

term.en: to address / to go into detail

short.en: to elaborate on

def.en: In the cover letter, you should directly address the requirements of the advertisement instead of just using general phrases.

short.en: to expect something good

def.en: From the new further training, I hope for better career opportunities in the company without spending extra money for it.

short.en: letter for job application

def.en: The cover letter is the first page of an application, in order to explain the interest in the job.

short.en: all documents for the job

def.en: I need to check my application documents one more time in order to avoid mistakes before sending them as a PDF.

short.en: main professional strength

def.en: My core competence lies in the precise creation of technical sketches and plans.

short.en: time spent working

def.en: Although I know the theory, I still lack practical professional experience in Germany.

short.en: flexible working time

def.en: I can flexibly start my workday in the morning between 7 and 9 a.m. because our company has introduced a flextime model.

short.en: desired earnings

def.en: Always state your salary expectations as a gross annual amount in the application.

short.en: data for tax purposes

def.en: Today, the income tax card is electronic (ELStAM) and is transmitted directly from the tax office to the boss.

short.en: category for income tax

def.en: Which tax class you have (1 to 6) depends heavily on your marital status.

short.en: ends on a fixed date

def.en: Due to the limitation, the contract ends after exactly one year unless it is extended.

short.en: payment according to collective agreement

def.en: Due to collective bargaining coverage, a fair minimum salary is guaranteed for all employees in the sector.

short.en: protection in case of illness

def.en: In Germany, insurance is compulsory, so you must be a member of a health insurance scheme.

short.en: help in case of job loss

def.en: Anyone who has paid in for a year receives money from the unemployment insurance upon termination (Arbeitslosengeld I).

short.en: accident insurance by the boss

def.en: In the event of an accident directly at the workplace, the employers liability insurance association helps; in doing so, it also covers the treatment costs.

short.en: proof of wages

def.en: Every month, the accounting department sends the payslip, on which all deductions are precisely listed.

short.en: legal rules against dismissal

def.en: The larger the company, the more reliably the legal protection against dismissal for employees takes effect after six months.

short.en: e-mail element

def.en: Do not forget to attach your certificates as an attachment to the e-mail in order to avoid follow-up questions.

short.en: a text in which a company describes an open position

def.en: Both in daily newspapers and on job portals you can find job advertisements today.

short.en: a website where you can search for and find jobs

def.en: Neither in the newspaper nor at the employment office – it is mainly on job portals that most open positions are found today.

short.en: all documents sent when applying for a job

def.en: A convincing job application includes both a cover letter and a CV and relevant certificates.

short.en: a limited period of gaining practical experience in a company

def.en: Internships do offer valuable practical experience, but they are often unpaid or poorly remunerated.

short.en: to start your own business and no longer work for someone else

def.en: She wanted either to find a permanent position in a corporation or to become self-employed – in the end she chose the second path.

short.en: a difficult task that requires a lot of effort and skill

def.en: The greatest challenge is that one must demonstrate both professional qualifications and social skills.

short.en: a response stating that you will not receive the position or appointment

def.en: The rejection was admittedly disappointing, but it gave him the opportunity to prepare better for the next job interview.

short.en: a positive response, e.g. that you will receive the position

def.en: After a long wait the eagerly awaited offer finally arrived, and he accepted it not only because of the salary but also because of the development opportunities.

short.en: an online platform where people maintain contacts and share information

def.en: Both for private communication and for job searching, social networks play a decisive role today.

short.en: an office or organisation that helps people find a job

def.en: The public job placement service helps both with job searching and with applications and qualification measures.

short.en: connector that links two positive aspects

def.en: The company values <g>both</g> professional competence <g>and</g> teamwork skills in new employees.

short.en: connector that adds a second, often stronger aspect to a statement

def.en: A good cover letter shows <g>not only</g> professional qualifications <g>but also</g> the applicantʼs personality and motivation.

short.en: connector linking two negative aspects – neither applies

def.en: The job interview went well, even though he could show <g>neither</g> professional experience in the sector <g>nor</g> specific certificates.

short.en: connector showing that as one thing increases or decreases, the other changes too

def.en: <g>The more</g> professional experience an applicant brings, <g>the greater</g> their chances of a well-paid position.

short.en: connector for a choice between two options

def.en: After graduating he must decide: <g>either</g> he accepts the consulting firmʼs offer <g>or</g> he founds his own start-up.

short.en: connector that first concedes something and then raises a counter-point

def.en: The company does <g>admittedly</g> have a good reputation, <g>but</g> the salary is significantly below the industry average.

short.en: information about oneself such as name, address and date of birth

def.en: In the CV both the personal details and the professional experience must be presented clearly.

short.en: all stages of a person's education and work

def.en: The more structured the professional career path is presented in the CV, the more convincing the application appears to the employer.

short.en: practical vocational training in a company, often combined with vocational school

def.en: A completed vocational training offers not only practical work experience but also a recognised professional qualification.

short.en: knowledge and experience in using computer programmes and digital tools

def.en: In the modern working world, both solid IT skills and a willingness to learn new software are expected.

short.en: knowledge and ability in one or more foreign languages

def.en: The better an applicantʼs language skills are, the more attractive they are to internationally active companies.

short.en: good enough in a language to conduct difficult conversations and negotiations

def.en: She speaks not only proficient business English but also fluent French, which significantly increases her chances on the international job market.

short.en: able to speak a language very well and without major difficulties

def.en: <g>The more fluently</g> someone speaks a foreign language, <g>the more confidently</g> they come across in international meetings and negotiations.

short.en: the handwritten name of a person at the end of a document

def.en: For an online CV a digital image of the signature is often sufficient, but handwritten ones are still required for official contracts.

short.en: day, month and year of an event or document

def.en: In the tabular CV the date must be clearly stated both at the start and at the end of each professional position.

short.en: an official certificate or diploma at the end of training or a degree programme

def.en: A university degree is admittedly no guarantee of immediate employment, but it does open significantly more doors on the job market.

short.en: appearing trustworthy and professional

def.en: Both the photo and the formatting of a CV must appear professional so that the first impression on the employer is positive.

short.en: a CV in table format with dates on the left and information on the right

def.en: In Germany the tabular CV is the standard form because it is both clear and easy to compare.

short.en: the specific entry of day, month or year in a document

def.en: In the tabular CV the date entries must be given either in MM / YYYY format or as a full date – the main thing is that they are consistent.

short.en: the first language learnt at home as a child

def.en: In the CV one indicates both the native language and all foreign languages with the respective level.

short.en: the same throughout, without differences in style or format

def.en: Both the font size and the spacing in the CV must be consistent so that the document looks professional.

short.en: a fixed text at the end of an e-mail with name, contact details and company

def.en: A professional email signature contains not only the name and telephone number but also the position and, where applicable, a link to the company website.

short.en: a question asked because something has not yet been fully understood

def.en: In the case of ambiguities in a job advertisement it makes sense to ask a follow-up question either by e-mail or by telephone before sending the application.

short.en: a formal offer, usually in a business or commercial context

def.en: The offer from the first company was admittedly financially attractive, but it provided neither flexible working hours nor the option to work from home.

short.en: vocational training carried out simultaneously at a company and at vocational school

def.en: Many young people choose dual vocational training in order to gain practical experience and at the same time obtain a recognised qualification.

short.en: a degree programme combined with training or employment at a company

def.en: He chose the dual study programme instead of focusing exclusively on full-time study, and was thus able to gain professional experience during his studies.

short.en: a school for trainees where vocational theory is taught

def.en: At vocational school one learns theoretical foundations without losing sight of the practical side of the profession, since the company takes care of the practical part.

short.en: a place in a company where one can complete vocational training

def.en: Many young people apply for an apprenticeship place early in order not to start the new school year without a position.

short.en: a company that takes on and trains apprentices

def.en: The training company is responsible for training the apprentice in a practical way, instead of just letting them carry out simple tasks.

short.en: the money an apprentice receives monthly during training

def.en: The trainee allowance is regulated by law in order to ensure that all apprentices receive fair remuneration.

short.en: a profession where one works with hands and tools, e.g. carpenter or electrician

def.en: Many young people choose a skilled trade in order to learn a future-proof profession with good earning potential.

short.en: a person currently completing vocational training in a company

def.en: As an apprentice one must learn how the company works without having much prior knowledge – which is precisely what makes the training so valuable.

short.en: a new vocational training course for someone who wishes to learn a different profession

def.en: She decided on retraining as a care worker instead of continuing to work in her old, physically demanding profession.

short.en: construction expressing the purpose or goal of an action

def.en: He completed an internship <g>in order to</g> gain practical experience in marketing and improve his chances on the job market.

short.en: construction expressing that something is absent or not done while something else happens

def.en: He passed the job interview <g>without</g> preparing particularly intensively – which greatly impressed the HR manager.

short.en: construction in which one action replaces another – one does b instead of a

def.en: <g>Instead of</g> starting a second degree programme, she opted for practical further training that opened up immediate career opportunities.

short.en: something one wants to achieve or do

def.en: She completed several further training courses in order to reach her professional goal – a management position – as quickly as possible.

short.en: a school following initial training that offers advanced specialist education

def.en: He attended technical school in order to obtain a state-recognised master craftsman's title after his training.

short.en: an educational institution where one can study and obtain academic degrees

short.en: a systematic analysis of possible hazards at the workplace

term.en: to speak freely, to speak without notes

def.en: In the long term, prevention probably always pays off – even if the costs simply appear higher in the short term.

short.en: relating to the mind and emotional well-being

def.en: Remaining psychologically healthy is probably just as important as physical health – unfortunately it is still often neglected.

term.en: to deal with, to handle (+ dative)

short.en: to handle a situation or person in a particular way

def.en: How one deals with stress is probably very individual – there is simply no universal remedy.

short.en: a way of approaching a problem or task

def.en: There is probably no perfect approach to health management – but some are probably better than others.

short.en: a regular medical examination to detect illnesses at an early stage

def.en: Preventive check-ups are after all free of charge – one should feel free to use the offers regularly.

short.en: financial support that someone receives for specific expenses

def.en: Many health insurance funds offer a subsidy for sports programmes – just asking is probably always worthwhile.

short.en: a conversation with the boss about more money for the work

def.en: Before the salary negotiation, one should prepare well for the conversation and name concrete figures.

short.en: to get more money for the work

def.en: The management has agreed to the following step: it will raise the salary of all employees starting next month.

short.en: an increase in monthly salary, often after negotiations or good performance

def.en: She waited a long time for the salary increase before it was finally approved.

short.en: the first salary one gets in a new job

def.en: The starting salary usually depends on the applicant's professional experience and degree.

short.en: how much money one expects for the work

def.en: In the job interview, she was asked about her salary expectation, and it should relate to the industry.

short.en: how strong or weak one is in a conversation about money

def.en: Anyone with several job offers is in a clearly better negotiating position.

short.en: to give reasons for one's opinion

def.en: She was able to argue convincingly for higher pay by listing her achievements.

short.en: how much a service or a profession is normally worth

def.en: Before negotiating about salary, one should realistically assess one's own market value.

short.en: how well and how much someone achieves at work

def.en: The amount of the bonus depends directly on the individual performance of each employee.

short.en: extra money received in addition to the normal salary

def.en: The annual bonus is based on the success of the entire company.

short.en: money received as a reward for good work

def.en: For the successful completion of the project, the team was paid an extra premium for special commitment.

short.en: extra benefits from the employer, for example insurance

def.en: Besides the salary, the company offers numerous social benefits that contribute to an attractive overall compensation package.

short.en: extra money one receives from the employer for the holiday

def.en: Holiday pay is usually paid out in June together with the normal salary; many employees already look forward to this bonus.

short.en: extra money one receives from the employer in december

def.en: Many collective agreements provide for a Christmas bonus in November in addition to the normal salary; employees then have a contractual entitlement to this payment.

short.en: money before deductions (gross) or after deductions (net)

def.en: The difference between gross and net results mainly from taxes and social security contributions.

short.en: an insurance that pays when one needs help in old age

def.en: The contribution to long-term care insurance is automatically deducted from the gross salary.

short.en: the part of the social security contributions that the employer pays

def.en: In addition to the employee's own contribution, the company also pays the employer's contribution to social security.

short.en: the part of the social security contributions that the employee pays

def.en: The employee's contribution is deducted directly from the gross wage and flows into the statutory insurance.

short.en: a level in the pay scale system that determines the salary

def.en: Classification into a certain pay grade depends on qualification and professional experience.

short.en: a salary that stays the same every month

def.en: Unlike variable remuneration, the fixed salary stays the same regardless of sales figures.

short.en: a part of the salary that depends on success

def.en: Variable remuneration is based on the revenue achieved and can differ every month.

short.en: a break from work to take care of a small child

def.en: During parental leave, the job is retained, because the employee has a right to return.

short.en: money from the state that one receives during parental leave

def.en: The application for parental allowance must be submitted to the responsible authority in good time.

short.en: when someone looks after children while the parents work

def.en: Good childcare considerably eases many parents' return to work.

short.en: when one can organise work and family well at the same time

def.en: Flexible working hours significantly improve the compatibility of work and family.

short.en: to organise work and family life at the same time

def.en: Thanks to working from home, she manages much better to combine work and family; she is proud of this balance.

short.en: the period before and after birth during which the mother is protected

def.en: During the maternity protection period, the employer may not require the employee to work.

short.en: a free place in a daycare centre or with a childminder

def.en: Without a childcare place for the child, many parents cannot return to their job.

short.en: work with fewer hours than a full position

def.en: After parental leave, she opted for part-time work in order to spend more time with the child.

short.en: when one resigns from the job oneself, not the employer

def.en: In the case of voluntary resignation, one must reckon with a possible waiting period for unemployment benefit.

short.en: when the job is ended immediately, without a notice period

def.en: Instant dismissal is legally permissible only for a particularly serious reason.

short.en: when the job is ended with the normal notice period

def.en: In the case of regular dismissal, the employer must adhere to the statutory notice period.

short.en: a document about one's work received during a job, not at the end

def.en: Before changing departments, she asked her supervisor for an interim reference.

short.en: to speak about someone in a friendly and positive way

def.en: A good employment reference should always be formulated in a benevolent tone.

short.en: a one-off payment made by an employer to an employee upon termination of employment

def.en: In the social plan, a generous severance pay was agreed for all affected employees.

short.en: when both sides are satisfied with a decision

def.en: The employment contract was terminated by mutual agreement, so no lawsuit before the labour court was necessary.

short.en: when one no longer has to work but still receives money

def.en: After the termination, there was a release from work duties until the last day of the contract.

short.en: a state office that helps people find a job

def.en: After termination, one must register as unemployed with the employment agency in order to receive money.

short.en: the right to receive money when one has no job

def.en: Anyone who has worked for at least twelve months usually acquires the right to unemployment benefit.

short.en: a period during which one receives no unemployment benefit because one resigned oneself

def.en: Anyone who resigns without good reason must reckon with a waiting period of up to twelve weeks.

short.en: the targeted reduction of the number of employees in a company

def.en: The company decided on extensive staff reduction in order to remain competitive.

short.en: the termination of an employment relationship by the employer

def.en: He was selected for redundancy on the grounds of operational reasons.

short.en: the reduction of the number of positions in a company

def.en: The job cuts in the IT department were attributable to pressure from shareholders.

short.en: fundamental changes in the organisation or processes of a company

def.en: The restructuring led to considerable changes in the entire staffing structure.

short.en: professional support for dismissed employees in finding a new job

def.en: The company offered outplacement counselling for all affected employees.

short.en: the transfer of a company or part of a business to a new owner

def.en: In a business transfer, all existing employment relationships pass to the new owner.

short.en: a written warning from the employer to the employee due to a breach of duty

def.en: A formal warning must be based on a specific breach of duty and be delivered to the employee in writing.

short.en: a statutory procedure in which social criteria are taken into account in job cuts

def.en: In social selection, attention is paid to criteria such as age, length of service and maintenance obligations.

short.en: the formal lodging of an objection against a decision

def.en: He lodged an objection against the dismissal and turned to the labour court.

short.en: a specialist court that decides disputes between employers and employees

def.en: The lawsuit was filed at the labour court and has now been admitted for hearing.

short.en: a hearing in which both sides attempt to resolve a dispute without a judgment

def.en: Both parties agreed on a settlement in the course of the settlement negotiations.

short.en: the area of law that regulates the relationship between employers and employees

def.en: The HR manager explained that the managers had to strictly observe the current German employment law when drafting new employment contracts in the factory.

short.en: the elected representation of employees in the public sector

def.en: The dismissal had been issued without consulting the staff council – that was unlawful.

short.en: a legally trained person who advises and represents others in legal matters

def.en: She turned to an experienced lawyer who specialised in employment law.

short.en: an official letter by which an employment relationship is terminated in writing

def.en: The written notice of termination must be delivered by registered post or in person to be legally effective.

short.en: an agreement between employer and works council regarding planned measures

def.en: The balancing of interests was negotiated between management and the works council.

short.en: progress in one's career, for example through promotions or new responsibilities

def.en: The HR manager said that an advancement to middle management had come after three years of hard work and had brought her both more responsibility and a significantly higher salary.

short.en: the conscious planning of one's own professional development with specific goals

def.en: The mentor told her that she should begin career planning early and record her goals in writing.

short.en: a specific professional goal that one wishes to achieve in the medium or long term

def.en: The manager emphasised that the career goal had to be realistic and measurable so that progress could be recognised.

short.en: an experienced person who supports a younger or less experienced person in their development

def.en: The colleague said that her mentor had helped her to clearly identify her strengths.

short.en: professional support in which a coach helps people to achieve personal and professional goals

def.en: The HR manager explained that coaching was not a sign of weakness but an investment in one's own development.

short.en: a meeting in which feedback on performance or behaviour is given

def.en: The team leader said that in the feedback meeting one should first listen before responding.

short.en: a regular official meeting between a manager and employee

def.en: The superior emphasised that the employee appraisal meeting should not be an interrogation but an open exchange.

short.en: a systematic assessment of an employee's work performance

def.en: The HR manager explained that the performance appraisal was based on measurable criteria and was transparent for everyone.

short.en: an agreement between a manager and employee on specific goals for a period

def.en: The superior said that the target agreement should be developed jointly and be binding for both sides.

short.en: opportunities to develop professionally or personally

def.en: The HR department announced that the development opportunities were equal for all employees and depended on performance.

short.en: an application for a vacant position within one's own company

def.en: The team leader explained that an internal application showed commitment and was often advantageous compared with external candidates.

short.en: a career path on which one becomes ever more specialised in a subject area without taking on staff responsibility

def.en: The coach said that a specialist career was more fulfilling for many experts than a management career.

short.en: a career path on which one progressively takes on staff responsibility and leads teams or departments

def.en: The HR manager emphasised that a management career required not only specialist competence but above all social skills.

short.en: the active building and maintaining of professional contacts

def.en: The mentor explained that networking was not a waste of time but a long-term investment in one's career.

short.en: the possible abilities or achievements that someone can still develop

def.en: The team leader said that he had high potential that had not yet been fully tapped.

term.en: to promote, to develop, to support

short.en: to actively support someone and help with their further development

def.en: The superior emphasised that it was his task to specifically develop talented employees.

short.en: the systematic identification, development and retention of particularly high-performing employees

def.en: The HR director explained that talent management aimed to identify key individuals at an early stage.

short.en: the preparation of qualified employees for future leadership positions

def.en: The managing director said that solid succession planning was crucial for the long-term stability of the company.

short.en: the continuous acquisition of new knowledge and skills across one's entire lifespan

def.en: The education expert emphasised that lifelong learning was not an option but a necessity in today's working world.

short.en: all measures designed to ensure that products or services meet certain standards

def.en: The department head explained that quality assurance was the responsibility of every employee and must not be neglected.

short.en: an accepted benchmark or minimum requirement that must be met

def.en: The quality officer explained that the standard for production processes was binding and had to be observed by all departments.

short.en: a binding rule or regulation that defines a particular behaviour or quality

def.en: The project manager emphasised that the norm was not an obstacle but a quality framework that made the work easier.

short.en: to officially confirm that something meets a particular norm or standard

def.en: The manager explained that the company wanted to have its production facility certified to ISO 9001 in order to ensure quality in a verifiable way.

short.en: a systematic review of processes or quality standards in a company

def.en: The quality officer reported that the audit had revealed that several processes urgently needed to be revised.

short.en: a sequence of steps or activities intended to achieve a specific goal

def.en: The team leader explained that the process of order processing was too complex and needed to be simplified.

short.en: to improve something so that it works as well as possible

def.en: The managing director said that the company wanted to fundamentally optimise the supply chain so that costs could be reduced and delivery times shortened.

short.en: a positive change through which something becomes better than before

def.en: The department head emphasised that the improvement of internal communication was crucial so that the team could work more efficiently.

short.en: a system of rules and procedures that ensures products or services meet a defined quality standard

def.en: The board explained that the quality management system was the foundation for ensuring that all production processes were reliable and traceable.

short.en: the percentage share of complaints or objections in relation to the total volume of deliveries or services

def.en: The quality manager reported that the complaint rate had fallen in the last quarter, which showed that the improvement measures were having an effect.

short.en: a document that clearly describes the tasks, duties and requirements of a specific position

def.en: The HR manager explained that the job description was not only important for recruitment but also served as a basis for performance appraisal.

short.en: a working time model in which employees can decide their own start and end times

def.en: The managing director reported that flexible working hours had significantly increased employee satisfaction because many colleagues could better reconcile family and work.

short.en: a model in which the employer does not monitor the hours worked but trusts employees

def.en: The team leader explained that trust-based working hours required all parties to be reliable and meant that results came first.

short.en: a balance between different areas, e.g. work and leisure, or compensation for something

def.en: The HR consultant said that a good balance between work and private life was crucial in the long run so that employees remained productive.

short.en: the percentage of employees unable to work due to illness

def.en: The company doctor explained that a high sick leave rate was often a signal that the working climate or working conditions needed to be improved.

short.en: measures intended to prevent people from becoming exhausted and burnt out through prolonged stress

def.en: The management consultant recommended that burnout prevention was not an optional extra but a strategic necessity so that the company remained competitive in the long term.

short.en: the general feeling of being well both physically and emotionally

def.en: The HR director emphasised that the well-being of employees was not a luxury but a prerequisite for the team being able to work productively on an ongoing basis.

short.en: the state of being emotionally stable and able to cope well with stress and challenges

def.en: The company doctor explained that the mental health of employees was just as important as physical health, and companies had to promote both equally.

short.en: the ability to recover quickly after difficulties, setbacks or stress

def.en: The coach emphasised that resilience was not an innate trait but a skill that could be deliberately trained and strengthened.

short.en: to clearly state or show what one accepts and what not, in order to protect one's own health or values

def.en: The psychologist advised that anyone who did not learn to set boundaries risked developing burnout in the long term and losing their ability to perform.

short.en: to mentally relax after work and clear one's head

def.en: The occupational psychologist said that many employees could barely switch off after work because the boundary between professional and private life was increasingly blurring.

short.en: the state in which one recovers physically and mentally after exertion and regains energy

def.en: The doctor emphasised that adequate rest after intensive work phases was not laziness but a biological necessity so that the brain remained able to perform.

short.en: a system that regulates when and how many hours employees work, e.g. flexitime or shift work

def.en: The works council explained that the new working time model should take into account both the needs of the workforce and the requirements of the company.

short.en: to take over work from an absent colleague at short notice

def.en: The team leader asked whether anyone was willing to stand in for the sick colleague tomorrow, as otherwise a shift would remain unstaffed.

short.en: a list showing who takes over a colleague's tasks in case of absence

def.en: The department head explained that the cover plan had to be kept up to date at all times so that no tasks were left unattended during holiday or illness.

short.en: a work model in which employees work alternately at different times of day, e.g. early, late or night shifts

def.en: The company doctor warned that rotating shifts placed a particularly heavy strain on the body, which was why regular check-ups were strongly recommended.

def.en: The union representative explained that on-call duty had to be compensated separately and must not fall below the statutory rest periods.

short.en: a person or arrangement that takes over an employee's tasks during their holiday

def.en: The colleague announced that she would be taking over holiday cover for two weeks and asked that all urgent queries be directed to her.

short.en: to exchange something mutually with someone, for example shifts or days off

def.en: He asked his colleague whether she was willing to swap the shift with him on Friday as he had an important medical appointment.

short.en: work that goes beyond the contractually agreed working hours and is usually additionally compensated

def.en: The works council emphasised that overtime may only be ordered with the employee's consent and must be compensated by time off or pay no later than the following month.

short.en: a person who does something of their own free will and without compulsion, e.g. voluntarily takes on a shift

def.en: The shift supervisor asked whether there was anyone willing to volunteer to cover the weekend, as two colleagues had dropped out at short notice.

short.en: the quality of an employer offering working conditions that allow a good balance between career and family life

def.en: The HR director reported that the company's family-friendliness was a key argument in the competition for qualified specialists.

short.en: a system of measures that a company uses to promote the health and well-being of its employees

def.en: The board decided that occupational health management should in future include not only sports programmes but also psychological counselling and ergonomic workplaces.

def.en: She reported that the salary negotiation had gone very constructively and her superior had agreed to a five per cent increase from the next quarter.

short.en: an additional payment that employees receive for particularly good performance or for achieving specific targets

short.en: a one-off additional payment outside the regular salary, e.g. christmas bonus or anniversary bonus

def.en: HR announced that every employee would receive a special payment at Christmas this year, provided the annual targets had been met.

short.en: an employer-supported savings plan for retirement that is built up in addition to the state pension

def.en: He announced that he had already submitted his notice of termination and would leave the company at the end of the month to start a new position.

short.en: to officially end an employment relationship, either by the employee or the employer

def.en: She said she wanted to resign at the end of the year because she had received a more attractive offer and was looking for new professional challenges.

short.en: to reach a higher position in the professional hierarchy

def.en: He claimed that he would advance within a year, as his manager had already recommended him for a leadership position and the decision was imminent.

short.en: the official transfer of an employee to a higher position with more responsibility and usually higher pay

def.en: The boss announced that his promotion would take effect from the next month and would include not only a higher salary but also leadership of his own team.

short.en: to be moved to a better position by a higher authority

def.en: He proudly said that he had been promoted after only one year because his quarterly results had been convincing and he had always taken on more responsibility.

short.en: a metaphor for the various levels of career advancement that one can climb in the course of one's career

def.en: She said that the career ladder in this corporation was quite steep, but anyone who was willing to consistently perform and build networks could climb it.

short.en: an official document that an employer issues to an employee at the end of employment, assessing their performance

def.en: The former employer confirmed that the employment reference had already been signed and would be delivered by registered post within the next few days.

short.en: involving a great deal of time, money or effort

def.en: The advisor explained that switching pension funds was time-consuming and required numerous documents as well as several weeks of processing time.

term.en: without a specific form, in free form

def.en: She explained that the enclosure with the application had to include proof of salary for the last three months, as otherwise the application could not be processed.

short.en: with effect for a period already in the past, as if a rule had already come into force earlier

short.en: of the same value, quality or rank as something else

term.en: to seek advice, to get counselling

short.en: to seek professional advice from an expert before making an important decision

short.en: the legal relationship between employer and employee established by an employment contract

def.en: The lawyer explained that the employment relationship would only end after the agreed notice period had expired and continued until then with all rights and obligations.

term.en: to believe someone is capable of something

short.en: to believe or be convinced that someone is able to handle a particular task or challenge

short.en: a collection of all important documents about an employee, maintained by the employer

short.en: a look back at past events or achievements in order to draw conclusions

short.en: a look at future developments or expectations, often as part of a meeting or report

short.en: the result and quality of work done, which can be assessed and compared against targets

def.en: The boss said that his work performance had clearly improved in the last quarter, which was why she considered a salary adjustment justified.

short.en: something that will happen in the near future and is usually already known or planned

def.en: She mentioned that the upcoming restructuring would also affect her department and that several positions could be eliminated or newly filled.

term.en: to treat confidentially, to keep confidential

short.en: to keep information secret and discreet and not pass it on to unauthorised third parties

def.en: The boss asked her to treat the information about the planned restructuring confidentially and under no circumstances to pass it on to colleagues outside the project.

short.en: to provide money to make something possible or to pay for it

term.en: to further qualify oneself, to upskill

short.en: to deliberately expand one’s professional knowledge and skills through further training

def.en: She said she wanted to further qualify herself alongside her job in order to improve her career prospects and become eligible for a management position in the long term.

short.en: directed at a concrete goal and suitable for actually achieving it

short.en: to be convinced of oneself and one’s own abilities and to show this outwardly

term.en: to be worth it, to pay off

short.en: to be worth the effort or risk because one benefits from it or gains an advantage

short.en: fitting, sensible or expected in a given situation

def.en: She said that a polite but firm tone was indeed appropriate in a salary negotiation, as modesty alone rarely led to a pay rise.

short.en: important for a particular situation or question and directly related to it

term.en: to create the impression, to give the impression

short.en: to evoke a particular impression in others through one’s behaviour or words

term.en: to raise expectations, to create expectations

short.en: to cause others to hope or expect that something particular will happen

def.en: The advisor warned that one should not raise expectations too high, as this could lead to disappointments later if the actual pay rise fell short of the promises.

short.en: a new idea that someone wants to use later to start their own company

term.en: setting up a business, start-up founding

short.en: the step where someone officially starts their own business

short.en: a written document that describes the business idea, costs, and chances of success of a new company

def.en: The bank demanded a detailed business plan before it was even willing to negotiate the amount of a possible loan.

short.en: the money someone already owns and invests in a company, without borrowing it from the bank

def.en: It's true that she had some equity capital, but it was nowhere near enough for setting up the business, so she also had to apply for a loan.

short.en: a person who works at a bank and advises customers on loans, accounts, or investments

short.en: a larger sum of money that someone borrows – usually from a bank – and repays according to a fixed plan

def.en: The finally approved loan allowed the young entrepreneur to purchase the first machines for his workshop.

short.en: to borrow money from a bank that must be paid back later

def.en: Whoever wants to take out a loan should carefully compare the terms of several banks.

short.en: the specific amount of money someone receives as a loan

def.en: The higher the loan amount, the more strictly the bank checks the available collateral and the monthly income.

short.en: the period during which a loan or contract is valid and must be repaid

short.en: the extra money someone has to pay a bank for a loan

def.en: In order to keep the interest as low as possible, she deliberately chose a shorter term.

short.en: a payment where a larger amount is paid not all at once but in several parts

short.en: the gradual repayment of a borrowed sum of money

def.en: After ten years of regular payments, the loan was completely repaid, so the repayment was officially complete.

short.en: a person who works independently in a liberal profession, e.g. as a doctor, lawyer, or journalist

short.en: a self-employed person who runs their business entirely alone, without employees of their own

def.en: Many solo self-employed people report that what they miss most in everyday work is the lack of exchange with colleagues.

short.en: the systematic recording of working hours

short.en: an employee's move to another department or location

def.en: HR explained that a transfer without the works council's approval was not permitted.

short.en: to move someone to another department or branch

def.en: The boss transferred the colleague to the branch office at short notice.

short.en: any work through which one earns money

def.en: The statistics showed that women's employment had increased significantly over the last ten years.

term.en: to pay according to the collective wage agreement

short.en: to pay wages according to the applicable collective agreement

def.en: This company pays its employees according to the collective wage agreement.

short.en: the money one earns through work

def.en: The report found that the average income had barely risen last year.

short.en: the money one receives for one's work

def.en: Many employees complained that the pay in this industry was too low compared to the workload.

short.en: the wage calculated per hour or per month

def.en: The new contract stipulated that the hourly wage would be increased by two euros starting in January.

short.en: the wage before deducting taxes and social security contributions
