a3.en: <r>One argument against that is</r> that you yourself are pretty overloaded right now and would hardly have time for a mentorship.

q4.en: <r>That's true, but</r> <r>we could perhaps solve the problem by</r> splitting the mentorship between the two of us.

a4.en: <r>I completely agree with you</r>. <r>Okay, so here's what I'll do</r>: I'll take the first two weeks, and after that you take over.

q5.en: Good. <r>Please make sure</r> you show him the basic functions first, then the more complex analyses - step by step.

a5.en: <r>Alright, so I need to</r> explain the basics first and also make sure he really understands everything before we move on.

q6.en: Exactly. And <r>it's also really important that</r> the mentorship gets officially set up in the contract, so there are no misunderstandings later.

a6.en: That makes sense. Will you take care of clarifying that with HR?

q7.en: Yes, would it be realistic if I bring it up already this afternoon?

a7.en: That should be feasible, as long as HR is still reachable today.

q8.en: Let's summarize: we'll take care of the login credentials, split the mentorship between us, and have it officially set up, so Mr. Fischer gets off to a good start in his new role.

a8.en: Exactly. I think that way he'll have a clear structure from the start and know who to turn to. I'll write to IT right away about the login credentials. <r>Let's also sit down together again in a week to see how he's settling in.</r>

task.en: Topic: Leisure time – „What do you actually enjoy doing in your free time?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually enjoy doing in your free time?

a.en: I've been playing guitar in a band for a few years now, that's actually my favorite hobby. We usually rehearse on Tuesday evenings. What about you, do you have a hobby you do regularly too?

q1.en: Yes, I really love climbing, ideally outdoors in summer, but in the climbing gym in winter too. How long have you actually been playing guitar?

a1.en: Since my school days, so probably fifteen years. Climbing sounds exciting too though - aren't you actually scared of it?

q2.en: At first a little, but by now I feel very safe with it, especially because I'm always out with experienced people. Do you and the band actually ever perform live?

a2.en: Yes, a few times a year, usually at smaller events in the city. It's a lot of fun, even though I'm always pretty nervous beforehand.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „Do you already have plans for your next vacation?“

q.en: Tell me, do you already have plans for your next vacation?

a.en: Yes, in August I'm flying to Portugal for two weeks, to the coast. I'm really looking forward to just switching off for a while. What about you, are you going anywhere this year too?

q1.en: I'm not quite sure yet, but I'm thinking about whether to go back to the mountains or try something completely new this time. Have you been to Portugal before?

a1.en: No, this is actually my first time there. A colleague really recommended it to me, because of the beaches and the good food. Do you actually prefer traveling alone or with family on vacation?

q2.en: Mostly with my partner, but this year we're thinking about maybe also traveling with friends for a few days. How long are you away in total?

a2.en: Exactly two weeks, that's usually enough <g>to</g> really unwind. But after that I'm honestly already a little looking forward to work again too.

task.en: Topic: Sports activities – „Do you actually exercise regularly?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually exercise regularly?

a.en: Yes, I've been going jogging three times a week since last year, usually early in the morning before work. It really gives me energy for the whole day. What about you, do you do any sport too?

q1.en: I go to yoga twice a week, it really helps me switch off after work. Do you actually run outside or do you prefer the treadmill?

a1.en: Almost always outside, except in really bad weather. I just like seeing a bit of nature while I do it. How long have you been doing yoga?

q2.en: About two years now, I started after a stressful time at work. Have you actually ever taken part in a race or a marathon?

a2.en: Yes, last year I did my first half marathon, that was a real challenge, but also really motivating. This year I might even try it again.

task.en: Topic: Working hours – „How are your working hours actually arranged?“

q.en: Tell me, how are your working hours actually arranged? Do you have fixed hours or flextime?

a.en: I have flextime, I usually start around half past eight and finish around half past five. That suits me well, because I don't get out of bed that early in the morning anyway. What's it like for you?

q1.en: It's similar for me, but I usually start already at eight, so I'm done earlier in the afternoon. Do you actually sometimes use the flextime for personal appointments too?

a1.en: Yes, gladly, last week for example I had a doctor's appointment in the morning and just made up the time in the evening. Do you actually sometimes work overtime?

q2.en: Every now and then, especially when a project is close to its deadline. But usually I can take the hours off again later. Do you actually sometimes work from home too?

a2.en: Yes, two days a week, usually Mondays and Fridays. I find that really practical, especially because I save the commute and can work more focused.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „How do you actually organize childcare alongside work?“

q.en: Tell me, how do you actually organize childcare alongside work? I imagine that's pretty stressful.

a.en: Honestly, it can be a real challenge sometimes. My daughter is at daycare in the mornings, and my mother usually steps in during the afternoon if I still have to work. Do you actually have kids yourself?

q1.en: No, not yet, but my sister has a two-year-old son, and I see how much organizing that takes. Is the daycare actually open all day?

a1.en: Yes, thankfully until five p.m., that usually fits pretty well with my working hours. It only really gets tight when I have to work longer sometimes. Does anyone in your family actually help with your niece or nephew?

q2.en: Yes, my parents step in every now and then when my sister has an appointment. I really love seeing how the whole family sort of holds together. Do you actually sometimes deliberately make time just for yourself?

a2.en: Honestly, rarely, but I try to at least keep one evening a week free just for myself. I just need that <g>to</g> recharge my energy.

task.en: Topic: Commute – „How do you actually usually get to work?“

q.en: Tell me, how do you usually get to work actually? Do you live far from the office?

a.en: Actually not that far, I mostly drive, it takes about twenty minutes. But sometimes I also take an e-scooter when the weather's good. What about you, what's it like for you?

q1.en: I actually drive almost always too, but recently I've been carpooling with a colleague from the neighborhood. How do you actually find the e-scooter compared to the car?

a1.en: It's really fun, especially in summer, but of course I don't use it when it rains. Carpooling sounds practical too though - does it save you a lot of costs?

q2.en: Yes, quite a lot actually, we split the gas and parking fees, and I only really have to drive every other week. Are there actually a lot of parking spots near you?

a2.en: Unfortunately not really, in the mornings I sometimes have to look for a free spot for quite a while. That's actually why I've been thinking for a while about riding the e-scooter more often, or even a bike.

task.en: Topic: Weekend – „What do you actually have planned for this weekend?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually have planned for this weekend?

a.en: I've actually been wanting to repaint my living room for a long time, so I'll probably use the weekend for that. It's bound to be exhausting, but I'm already looking forward to how it'll look afterward. What about you, have you planned anything yet?

q1.en: I'm meeting an old friend on Saturday whom I haven't seen in ages. We want to go for brunch together and then maybe do some shopping. What color have you actually picked for your living room?

a1.en: I'm still deciding between a light gray and a warm beige, but I just can't make up my mind. Sounds nice though that you two are meeting up again after so long - what do you usually talk about then?

q2.en: Actually about all sorts of things, but mostly about work or what's going on with each of us right now. On Sunday though I really don't want to do anything and just relax. Do you actually have an idea yet how you'll wind down the weekend?

a2.en: On Sunday I'll probably just lie on the couch and watch a series, after I've completely worn myself out with the painting.

task.en: Topic: Leisure time – „What do you actually like doing most when you have a bit of time for yourself?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually like doing most when you have a bit of time for yourself?

a.en: I've been going to a painting class for a few months now, that's been a dream of mine for a long time. We meet every Wednesday evening and paint together with acrylics. What about you, how do you like to spend your free time most?

q1.en: I'm actually in a book club, we read a new book every month and then meet up <g>to</g> discuss it. Have you actually gotten pretty good at painting already, or are you just starting out?

a1.en: I'd say I'm making progress, even though I'm still far from a professional. A book club sounds really exciting too though - what book are you reading right now?

q2.en: Right now we're reading a crime novel set in Berlin, it's really fun. Do you actually exhibit your paintings anywhere, or do you just paint for yourself?

a2.en: So far just for myself, but a few people from the class did a small exhibition last year. Maybe I'll work up the courage to do that too someday.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „Do you actually already have plans for the summer?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually already have plans for the summer? Are you going anywhere on vacation?

a.en: Yes, I'm taking a camper van through Norway for a week, I've wanted to do that for a long time. I'm really looking forward to the nature there and the many fjords. What about you, do you have anything planned too?

q1.en: I think I'll actually stay home this year and do a kind of staycation, so just a few free days without any concrete plans. Have you actually traveled by camper van before?

a1.en: No, this is actually my first time, I'm already a bit excited about how it'll turn out. A staycation sounds really relaxing too though - what do you usually do on days off like that?

q2.en: Mostly I just sleep in and meet up with friends who also have time then. Sometimes I also spontaneously drive somewhere for a day. How long are you actually traveling by camper van?

a2.en: Exactly one week, in my opinion that's just about right <g>to</g> see a few places <g>without</g> being totally stressed.

task.en: Topic: Sports activities – „Do you actually do sports, or not really?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually do sports, or not really?

a.en: Actually yes, I've been playing football since school, these days in a small recreational league here in the city. We train twice a week and usually have a match on the weekend. What about you, do you do anything sporty too?

q1.en: I actually go to the gym three times a week, mainly strength training. I find it really satisfying when you see yourself slowly getting stronger. How's it going with your league actually, are you doing well right now?

a1.en: Pretty well actually, we're currently in second place. Strength training sounds exciting too though - have you actually set yourself any concrete goals?

q2.en: Yes, I actually want to significantly increase my squat weight by the end of the year. That really motivates me to go regularly. Do you actually sometimes get injured playing football?

a2.en: Fortunately only minor things so far, but a teammate injured his knee last year and had to take a pretty long break. That's why I always warm up especially thoroughly these days.

task.en: Topic: Working hours – „What's it actually like for you with the working hours?“

q.en: Tell me, what's it actually like for you with the working hours? Do you work full-time or part-time?

a.en: I've been working part-time since last year, about thirty hours a week. That was a deliberate decision, so I'd have more time for myself. What about you, how is that arranged for you?

q1.en: I work full-time, but I have relatively flexible core hours. How did you actually negotiate reducing to part-time with your boss?

a1.en: That was actually easier than I thought, I just had to explain why I wanted it, and then we made a plan together. Do you actually sometimes miss having more days off?

q2.en: Honestly, a little bit, especially when I see how relaxed you seem. But I still need the salary of a full-time position right now. Do you actually wish you'd go back to full-time at some point?

a2.en: Not really at the moment, I just enjoy the extra time too much. But maybe that'll change again if my life situation changes.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „How do you actually handle childcare when you're both working?“

q.en: Tell me, how do you actually handle childcare when you're both working?

a.en: We actually split it up pretty well: I take the kids to school in the morning, and my partner usually picks them up in the afternoon. On the days he has to work longer, luckily the after-school club steps in. What about you, how does that work for you?

q1.en: For us it's similar, except we don't have a partner to share it with - I mostly do it alone, with support from my neighbor. How old are your kids actually?

a1.en: My daughter is seven and my son is ten, luckily they're both already relatively independent getting to school by now. That must be exhausting though, organizing all of that alone - do you actually get a lot of support from family?

q2.en: Fortunately yes, my parents live very close by and step in whenever things get tight. Without the two of them it would really be difficult. Do you actually sometimes take vacation days just <g>to</g> spend time with the kids?

a2.en: Yes, we do try to do that regularly, especially during school holidays. It's really important to both of us, even if it's sometimes hard to juggle with work.

task.en: Topic: Commute – „How long does it actually take you to get to work, and how do you get there?“

q.en: Tell me, how long does it actually take you to get to work, and how do you get there?

a.en: I actually walk, it takes about twenty-five minutes. Luckily I live pretty centrally, so <g>neither</g> a car <g>nor</g> the train is really worth it for me. What about you, what's it like for you?

q1.en: I take the bus, it usually takes about thirty minutes, but if there are delays it can even take an hour sometimes. Do you actually enjoy walking every day?

a1.en: Yes, totally, for me it's almost like a little walk to wake up. In the rain it's obviously less pleasant, but I gladly put up with that. Do you actually often get annoyed about the bus delays?

q2.en: Honestly, sometimes yes, especially when it makes me late for a meeting because of it. By now I've gotten used to always planning in a buffer. Do you actually also walk in really bad weather, or do you take a taxi then?

a2.en: No, I actually always walk, no matter the weather, I just have a good rain jacket. I prefer that to having to rely on a taxi or public transport.

task.en: Topic: Weekend – „Do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?

a.en: Yes, my niece's birthday is on Saturday, so we're celebrating at my sister's place in the garden, if the weather cooperates. I still need to get a present. What about you, what's on your agenda?

q1.en: I actually wanted to go to the farmers' market, it's only here on Saturdays, and maybe to a café afterward. Do you actually have an idea yet what you could give her?

a1.en: I'm thinking about whether to get her a book or maybe something for painting instead, she's really into being creative right now. The farmers' market sounds nice too though - do you actually shop there often?

q2.en: Yes, almost every week, I just like getting the vegetables and fruit fresh directly from the stalls. How old is your niece actually going to turn?

a2.en: She's turning six, time really does fly by. I'm already really looking forward to seeing all the kids play together at the party.

task.en: Topic: Leisure time – „What do you actually like doing most when you have free time?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually like doing most when you have free time?

a.en: I really love photography, usually on weekends I go out and look for beautiful subjects in nature. It really relaxes me. What about you, do you have a hobby that's important to you too?

q1.en: I love baking, especially sourdough bread, I've been doing that for over a year now. What do you actually like photographing most?

a1.en: Mostly landscapes, especially at sunrise or sunset, the light is just incredible then. Baking sourdough bread sounds exciting too though - isn't that pretty labor-intensive?

q2.en: At first it was, you have to feed the sourdough starter regularly, but by now it's become routine for me. Do you actually post your photos somewhere online, or do you keep them to yourself?

a2.en: I post something every now and then on a small account, mainly for friends and family. I just enjoy capturing the moments, even if not many people see it.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „Do you already have plans for your next vacation?“

q.en: Tell me, do you already have plans for your next vacation?

a.en: Yes, in the fall I'm flying to Vienna for a few days, I've never been there and have wanted to see the city for a long time. What about you, do you have anything planned too?

q1.en: I actually go visit my family in Poland, I do that almost every year in summer. Are you actually especially looking forward to something specific in Vienna?

a1.en: Totally, I definitely want to try the coffee houses there and maybe go to a concert too. Is it actually nice to visit family that regularly?

q2.en: Yes, very, even though the trip is sometimes a bit exhausting. But it's really worth it to see my grandparents and cousins again. Are you actually flying to Vienna alone, or is someone coming with you?

a2.en: I'm flying alone this time, I actually think it's quite nice to have time for myself now and then and explore everything at my own pace.

task.en: Topic: Sports activities – „Do you actually do sports regularly, or more irregularly?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually do sports regularly, or more irregularly?

a.en: I've been swimming twice a week for a few years now, usually early in the morning before there are a lot of people at the pool. It's really meditative for me. What about you, do you do sports too?

q1.en: I actually play tennis, once a week with a friend, and on Saturdays I sometimes go cycling too. Do you actually prefer swimming in the pool or in the lake?

a1.en: Actually both, in summer I really love going to the lake, that's even more relaxing than the pool. How long have you actually been playing tennis together?

q2.en: For over three years now, we're really well coordinated by now. Do you actually also ride longer distances by bike, or more short tours?

a2.en: Mostly short tours on the weekend, but last year I once rode a really long distance, that was a real challenge, but also really satisfying.

task.en: Topic: Working hours – „How are your working hours actually arranged?“

q.en: Tell me, how are your working hours actually arranged? Do you actually sometimes work shifts too?

a.en: Yes, actually, I work alternating early and late shifts, that changes weekly. At first that was pretty unusual for my rhythm. What about you, what's it like for you?

q1.en: I actually have pretty normal office hours, usually from nine to five. How do you actually cope with the constant switching between shifts?

a1.en: Pretty well by now, I've gotten used to fixed sleep routines, no matter which shift I'm currently on. Do you actually sometimes find your fixed office hours boring too?

q2.en: Sometimes, honestly, but I also appreciate the predictability, because I always know exactly when I have time off. Do you actually get a bonus for the late shift?

a2.en: Yes, fortunately, that at least financially compensates for the inconvenience a bit. Without the bonus, honestly, it would hardly be worth it.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „How is it actually with childcare for you now that your son is older?“

q.en: Tell me, how is it actually with childcare for you now that your son is older?

a.en: Honestly, it's actually getting easier, my son is fourteen now and manages pretty well on his own. I don't have to take him everywhere anymore, that really saves a lot of time. What about you, how do you handle it with your kids?

q1.en: Mine are still little, three and five, so it's still pretty demanding. We have a childminder who steps in twice a week. Do you actually sometimes miss the time when he was younger?

a1.en: Sometimes, honestly, but I also enjoy having more free time for myself again now. A childminder sounds practical though - how did you actually find her?

q2.en: Through a recommendation from friends, we got really lucky. Is your son actually home alone often already, or is someone with him?

a2.en: More often by now, but I still call in between sometimes, just <g>to</g> make sure everything's okay.

task.en: Topic: Commute – „How far is it actually to work for you? Do you commute a lot?“

q.en: Tell me, how far is it actually to work for you? Do you commute a lot?

a.en: Honestly, pretty far, I ride a motorcycle, it takes about forty-five minutes. In summer that's really fun, but in winter it's quite a challenge. What about you, what's your commute like?

q1.en: For me it's only ten minutes by tram, I'm really lucky to live so centrally. Do you actually also ride the motorcycle in winter, or do you switch then?

a1.en: In snow or ice I actually switch to the train, that's just too risky for me then. Ten minutes sounds really dreamy though - have you actually ever had a longer commute somewhere else?

q2.en: Yes, in my last job I had to travel an hour, that was pretty exhausting in the long run. That's why when I was looking for an apartment I deliberately chose to be close to work. Do you actually sometimes think about moving closer to work?

a2.en: Honestly, quite often, but I'm just too attached to my current apartment and the neighborhood <g>to</g> actually move.

task.en: Topic: Weekend – „Do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?

a.en: Yes, I've been volunteering at an animal shelter for a few months now, and on Saturdays I usually help there by walking the dogs. That really brings me joy. What about you, do you have plans already?

q1.en: I actually wanted to go hiking, there's a nice trail through the forest nearby that I've wanted to try for a long time. How did you actually come up with the idea of the animal shelter?

a1.en: A friend took me along once, and I've just stuck with it since. It's really nice to see how some dogs change after a few weeks. Do you actually go hiking alone, or do you take someone with you?

q2.en: Mostly alone, I find it really relaxing to just be out with my own thoughts. How many hours do you actually usually spend at the shelter?

a2.en: About three to four hours, that's usually enough <g>to</g> really make a difference, <g>without</g> it becoming too exhausting for me.

task.en: Topic: Leisure time – „What do you actually like doing most when you have free time?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually like doing most when you have free time?

a.en: I really love gardening, I've had a small allotment garden since last year and spend a lot of time there. Right now I'm planting tomatoes and herbs. What about you, how do you like to spend your free time most?

q1.en: I actually play a lot on the computer, mostly in the evenings online with friends. It really relaxes me after work. What do you actually grow in your garden?

a1.en: Mainly vegetables, but also a few flowers for the bees. I really enjoy seeing everything grow. Do you actually always play the same game, or do you switch often?

q2.en: Mostly the same one, we've been on a team together for years now, it's just more fun when you know each other well. Are you actually already harvesting anything from your garden, or is it still too early?

a2.en: I can already harvest the first herbs, but I still have to wait a few weeks for the tomatoes. But I'm already really looking forward to it.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „Do you actually already have plans for the winter vacation?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually already have plans for the winter vacation?

a.en: Yes, in January I'm going skiing in the Alps for a week, I actually do that every year with my siblings. What about you, do you have anything planned too?

q1.en: I think I'll rather stay home this year, honestly I'm not a big fan of the cold. Do you actually always go to the same ski resort, or do you switch sometimes too?

a1.en: We mostly go to the same area, because we already know the slopes really well there. Cold really isn't for everyone - what do you do instead when you stay home then?

q2.en: I usually use the time <g>to</g> really rest and maybe read a few books that have been sitting on my pile for a long time. Have you actually been skiing for a long time, or did you only learn as an adult?

a2.en: Since I was little, my parents basically put me on skis as soon as I could walk. That's why it's just a fixed part of winter for me.

task.en: Topic: Sports activities – „Do you actually do sports, or is that more not your thing?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually do sports, or is that more not your thing?

a.en: Actually yes, I've been dancing for a few years now, mainly salsa, I do that once a week in a class. It's really fun and you get to meet really nice people too. What about you, do you do anything sporty too?

q1.en: I actually do martial arts, specifically judo, I've been training that since my youth. How hard was it actually at first to learn the steps in salsa?

a1.en: Honestly, pretty hard at first, I had two left feet, but it really gets better over time. Judo sounds exciting too though - have you actually reached a certain belt rank yet?

q2.en: Yes, I'm at brown belt by now, but black is still quite a way off. Do you actually always dance with the same partner, or do you switch in the class?

a2.en: We actually switch constantly, that's just part of salsa somehow. At first that felt a bit awkward to me, but now I really enjoy it.

task.en: Topic: Working hours – „How are your working hours actually arranged?“

q.en: Tell me, how are your working hours actually arranged? Do you work the classic five days a week?

a.en: No, actually not, we introduced a four-day week a few months ago, so I only work Monday to Thursday now. What about you, what's it like for you?

q1.en: I actually still work the classic five days, but with relatively short days. How has the four-day week actually affected your productivity?

a1.en: Honestly, I've actually become more productive, because I concentrate more on the four days. Five shorter days sounds nice too though - how long do you actually work per day?

q2.en: Usually about six hours, that's completely enough for me. Do you actually earn just as much with the four-day week as before, or was the salary adjusted?

a2.en: Fortunately just as much, that was one of the most important conditions when it was introduced. Without full pay compensation, honestly, I wouldn't have gone along with it either.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „How do you actually handle childcare during the summer holidays?“

q.en: Tell me, how do you actually handle childcare during the summer holidays? That's six weeks without school after all.

a.en: Honestly, that's always the biggest challenge of the year. We send our daughter to a summer camp for three weeks, and split the rest of the time between my husband and me. What about you, how do you handle it?

q1.en: For us, my mother usually takes over for a few weeks, she's really happy to have her grandkids around longer. What does your daughter actually do at the summer camp, does she have a specific program?

a1.en: It's a sports camp, she does various activities there like swimming, climbing and ball games. She loves it and looks forward to it the whole year. How old are your grandkids actually - uh, I mean your kids?

q2.en: No problem, mine are six and nine. Have you actually ever worried that your daughter might get homesick at the camp?

a2.en: A little at first, but she settled in surprisingly quickly and hardly calls us, which is actually a good sign.

task.en: Topic: Commute – „How do you actually usually get to work? Do you have a fixed route?“

q.en: Tell me, how do you actually usually get to work? Do you have a fixed route?

a.en: Actually not really, it's quite different for me. Sometimes I take the subway, sometimes I ride with a ride-sharing app, depending on what fits best at the time. What about you, do you have a fixed commute?

q1.en: I actually always take the subway, that's the most reliable for me. How does it actually work with the ride-sharing app, do you always find someone quickly?

a1.en: Mostly yes, especially during rush hour there are a lot of people going the same route. It's also cheaper than driving alone by car. Do you actually sometimes ride a bike too, when the weather's good?

q2.en: Sometimes, but honestly I'm rather inconsistent about it, mostly I end up sticking with the subway anyway. Do you actually talk a lot with the people you ride with?

a2.en: Depends, sometimes I have a really good conversation with them, sometimes everyone just listens to their own music. Both are actually completely fine with me.

task.en: Topic: Weekend – „Do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually have anything planned for this weekend?

a.en: Yes, I finally want to assemble my new shelf, it's been sitting unpacked in my apartment for two weeks now. That'll probably take the whole Saturday. What about you, what are you up to?

q1.en: I actually wanted to go to the flea market, it takes place here once a month, and I've been looking for some old books for a long time. Is the shelf actually hard to assemble, or do you already have experience with that?

a1.en: Honestly, I'm not particularly skilled at it, but luckily a friend is helping me with it. Without him it would probably take forever. Do you actually often find what you're looking for at the flea market?

q2.en: Sometimes, but sometimes nothing at all too, it's always a bit of luck. What kind of shelf did you choose actually, a simple one or something fancier?

a2.en: Something fancier, it has lots of small compartments and looks really nice. That's why the assembly probably takes longer than with a normal shelf too.

task.en: Topic: Leisure time – „What do you actually like doing most when you have time for yourself?“

q.en: Tell me, what do you actually like doing most when you have time for yourself?

a.en: I've been doing pottery for a few months now, I found a class in a small workshop nearby. It's really meditative working with your hands. What about you, how do you like to spend your free time most?

q1.en: I actually really like playing chess, mostly online, but sometimes also with my grandpa, he's really good at it. What do you actually make with pottery?

a1.en: Mainly bowls and cups, but I'm also slowly trying my hand at more complicated shapes. Have you actually been playing chess for a long time, or did you only start recently?

q2.en: Since my childhood actually, my grandpa taught me when I was about eight. How long does it actually take until a cup like that is finished?

a2.en: From the first shaping to the finished firing it usually takes two to three weeks, because everything has to dry and be fired. That really requires quite a bit of patience.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „Do you actually already have plans for your next vacation?“

q.en: Tell me, do you actually already have plans for your next vacation?

a.en: Yes, in summer I'm going on a Mediterranean cruise for the first time, that's been my dream for a long time. I'm really looking forward to visiting different ports. What about you, do you have anything planned too?

q1.en: I actually wanted to backpack through Southeast Asia, really planless and spontaneous. What are you actually hoping for most from the cruise?

a1.en: Mostly that I can really relax <g>without</g> having <g>to</g> worry about anything. Everything's already organized after all. Backpacking sounds really exciting too though - have you actually done that before?

q2.en: Yes, a few years ago, that was one of the best experiences of my life. You really learn to get by with very little. How long does your cruise actually last?

a2.en: Two weeks, that's exactly the right length for me <g>to</g> really switch off, <g>without</g> it getting too long in the end.

task.en: I'd like to start climbing. What do you think?

q.en: Tell me, I'd like to start climbing. <r>What do you think</r>?

a.en: Yes, <r>I think that's a good idea</r>, it's supposed to be great for fitness. <r>Have you had any experience with it</r> already, or would that be completely new for you?

q1.en: Completely new, honestly. <r>I don't know, I'm not sure</r> if I'm brave enough for it. Do you think it's really as exhausting as everyone says?

a1.en: <r>It depends on whether</r> you start in a climbing gym or straight outdoors on real rock. In the gym it's much easier for beginners. <r>But you should just try it</r>.

q2.en: That's probably true. <r>What do you think</r>, should I rather start alone or right away together with someone?

a2.en: <r>I think that</r> it's easier at the start to go with someone experienced who shows you the basics. I could take you along sometime, for example, if you'd like.

task.en: Topic: Sport activities – „What could we do to stay more active during the workday?“

q.en: Tell me, what could we actually do to get more <g>movement</g> into the workday? I just sit at my desk all day.

a.en: <r>I think that's a good idea</r> to think about. <r>We could</r> maybe take a short walk during the lunch break, that already helps with <g>stress relief</g>.

q1.en: True, I sometimes already do that. <r>There's also the option</r> of taking the stairs instead of the elevator, right? Small things that fit easily into everyday life.

a1.en: Exactly, and some companies also offer relaxation exercises or a fitness room. <r>Would you have another idea</r> how we could do that as a team?

q2.en: <r>Maybe we could also</r> organize a team sports activity, for example yoga once a week after work. <r>What do you think</r>, would that appeal to our colleagues?

a2.en: <r>I think that</r> a lot of people would enjoy that, especially for <g>preventing</g> back pain. <r>That would be my suggestion</r>: let's just ask the boss about it.

task.en: Topic: Working hours – „I'd like to work from home more often. What do you think?“

q.en: Tell me, I'd like to work from home more often. <r>What do you think</r>?

a.en: Yes, <r>I think so too</r>, especially on days when you need to concentrate, it's really practical. Have you talked to your boss about it yet?

q1.en: Not directly yet, but I'm thinking about it. <r>I don't know, I'm not sure</r> if that would even be possible in our team. How do you actually handle that in your department?

a1.en: For us it's pretty flexible now – we can choose two days a week freely. <r>It depends on whether</r> there are important meetings coming up, but otherwise it works well.

q2.en: That sounds good. <r>What do you think</r>, should I rather apply in writing or bring it up informally first?

a2.en: <r>I'd recommend</r> asking informally first, that feels less formal. If she's open to it, you can put it in writing later.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „What could be done to make it easier to combine work and childcare?“

q.en: Tell me — <g>just</g> out of curiosity — what could actually be done to make it easier to combine work and childcare? How do you <g>actually</g> manage that with your kids?

a.en: That's a good question. <r>We could maybe</r> offer more flexible working hours, then people could take their kids to school themselves in the morning.

q1.en: True, that would be a good start. <r>There's also the option</r> of the company offering an on-site daycare, right?

a1.en: Yes, exactly, some bigger companies already offer that. <r>Would you have another idea</r> how to make everyday life easier?

q2.en: <r>Maybe we could also</r> work from home when a child is sick. <r>What do you think</r>, would that work at your place?

a2.en: <r>I think that</r> would definitely help. It'll work out <g>just fine</g> if you talk to your boss openly about it.

task.en: Topic: Vacation – „I'd like to take short getaways more often instead of one long trip a year. What do you think?“

q.en: Tell me, I'd like to take short getaways more often instead of one long trip a year. <r>What do you think</r>?

a.en: Yes, <r>I think so too</r>, that way you have something to look forward to more often throughout the year. <r>Have you had any experience with that</r>?

q1.en: Yes, last year I went away twice for a long weekend, that was really relaxing. Do you do that more often too?

a1.en: So far rather rarely, I usually take one big vacation in summer. <r>It depends on whether</r> I have enough vacation days left for something spontaneous like that.

q2.en: I understand. <r>What do you think</r>, would it be worth splitting up the annual leave?

a2.en: I think so, especially <g>to</g> really switch off in between. I'll definitely try that out next year.

task.en: Topic: Commute – „What could be done to make the commute to work less stressful?“

q.en: Tell me, what could actually be done to make the commute to work less stressful? I'm stuck in <g>backed-up</g> traffic every morning.

a.en: <r>I think that's a good idea</r> to think about. <r>We could maybe</r> cycle more often, especially with <g>rising</g> fuel prices that's worth it.

q1.en: True, I sometimes already do that in summer. <r>There's also the option</r> of forming a carpool, right?

a1.en: Yes, exactly, that would also ease the growing traffic jams on the highway a bit. <r>Would you have another idea</r>?

q2.en: <r>Maybe we could also</r> leave earlier to avoid the worst rush-hour traffic. <r>What do you think</r>, would that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I think that</r> would definitely help. With a well-<g>planned</g> time buffer, you arrive much more relaxed.

task.en: Topic: Leisure activities – „I'd like to do a course or workshop more often on weekends instead of just staying home. What do you think?“

q.en: Tell me, I'd like to do a course or workshop more often on weekends instead of just staying home. <r>What do you think</r>?

a.en: Yes, <r>I think so too</r>, you always learn something new that way. <r>Have you had any experience with that</r>?

q1.en: Yes, last year I did a pottery course, that was really fun. Do you sometimes do something like that too?

a1.en: So far rather rarely, I usually just spend weekends with friends. <r>It depends on whether</r> I feel like trying something new or would rather relax.

q2.en: I get that. <r>What do you think</r>, would you be interested in trying a cooking class together sometime?

a2.en: I think so, that sounds like a good idea. Let's give it a try next weekend.

task.en: Topic: Weekend – „What could you do on a rainy weekend?“

q.en: Tell me, what could you actually do on a rainy weekend? I often have no idea what to do when the weather's that bad outside.

a.en: <r>I think that's a good idea</r> to think about. <r>We could maybe</r> go to the cinema, <g>because of</g> the bad weather that's actually perfect.

q1.en: True, I sometimes do that too. <r>There's also the option</r> of just baking at home, right?

a1.en: Yes, exactly, I really like doing that <g>during</g> the rain, it's really cozy. <r>Would you have another idea</r>?

q2.en: <r>Maybe we could also</r> go to a museum, <g>despite</g> the weather it's all dry in there. <r>What do you think</r>, would you like that?

a2.en: <r>I think that</r> would be a great idea. Let's just try that out on the next rainy weekend.

task.en: Topic: Childcare – „I'd like to keep working part-time after parental leave. What do you think?“

q.en: Tell me, I'd like to keep working part-time after parental leave. <r>What do you think</r>?

a.en: Yes, <r>I think so too</r>, that way you can combine family and work better. Have you talked to your boss about it yet?

q1.en: Not yet, but I'm thinking about it. <r>I don't know, I'm not sure</r> how many hours I could realistically manage.

a1.en: I understand that. <r>It depends on whether</r> your daycare also offers flexible hours, right?

q2.en: Exactly, that's not clear yet for us unfortunately. <r>What do you think</r>, should I talk to the daycare first or to my employer?

a2.en: <r>I'd recommend</r> clarifying the daycare question first, then you can suggest specific hours to your employer.

task.en:
In your team, the weekly meetings regularly run much longer than planned. Colleagues often interrupt each other, and not all agenda items get covered.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Time frame: How can meetings be finished on time?
Speaking time: How can you prevent everyone from interrupting each other?
Agenda: How can you make sure all items get covered?
Moderation: Who should lead the meeting?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: our weekly team meetings almost always take much longer than planned now, and we often don't manage to cover every item on the agenda.

a.en: <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so the main issue is that we're not managing our time well enough during the meeting?

q1.en: Exactly, and on top of that, some people keep interrupting each other before anyone can finish their thought. <r>What options do you see</r> for changing that?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could set a fixed speaking time for each agenda item, say five minutes. <r>What do you think about that</r>?

q2.en: <r>That sounds reasonable</r>. <g>Whoever</g> goes over their speaking time should be reminded politely, right?

a2.en: Yes, exactly, the person moderating the meeting could take care of that, for example. Who usually moderates in your team, actually?

q3.en: No one really, so far we just start. <r>Maybe it would make sense if</r> we took turns moderating?

a3.en: <r>I think that's a good idea, though we should also keep in mind that</r> the person moderating needs to prepare well beforehand so the agenda is actually followed.

q4.en: True. <r>How about if we</r> send out the agenda a day in advance, so everyone can prepare?

a4.en: <r>I agree with that</r>. And <g>whoever</g> wants to bring up additional points can let the person moderating know beforehand.

q5.en: Good, then <r>we could</r> also set a fixed meeting length of 45 minutes, so we all stick to it.

a5.en: <r>I think that's a good suggestion</r>. If a topic needs more time, we could just schedule a separate appointment for it instead of extending the meeting.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll introduce a fixed speaking time, rotating moderation, and an agenda sent out in advance, and meetings should be a maximum of 45 minutes going forward.

a6.en: Exactly. I think that will make our meetings a lot more efficient. I'll put the new rules together and send them to the whole team today.

task.en:
For some time now there's been tension in your team between two colleagues: one of them feels constantly interrupted during meetings, and her suggestions are barely taken seriously. As a result, the mood in the team is noticeably tense.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Conversation: How can you bring up the topic without putting anyone on the spot?
Causes: What might be causing the conflict?
Rules: What rules could prevent interruptions in meetings?
Follow-up: How can you make sure the situation actually improves?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: <r>I've noticed that</r> things have been pretty tense between Sarah and Tom lately. Sarah told me she feels constantly interrupted by him in meetings.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: she feels her suggestions aren't really being heard because of that?

q1.en: Exactly, and it's really weighing on her. <r>What could we do in this situation</r> <g>without</g> it becoming uncomfortable for everyone?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: maybe we could talk to Tom privately first, <g>instead of</g> bringing it up in front of the whole team right away.

q2.en: I think that's good. <r>I can understand that</r> he's probably not even aware of it. <r>What do you think if</r> we just tell him: 'We've noticed that...'?

a2.en: Yes, <r>that sounds reasonable</r>. We should also tell him that his behavior is uncomfortable for the team, but without making accusations.

q3.en: Good idea. On top of that, we could suggest introducing fixed meeting rules, for example letting each other finish speaking.

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>. We could also introduce a small note or signal for when someone gets interrupted.

q4.en: And how do we make sure this actually improves and isn't forgotten again after a few days?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> just bring the topic up again in a few weeks and ask both of them how things are going.

q5.en: Good point. Should we have the conversation with Tom this week, so the situation doesn't escalate further?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could take care of that, if you talk to Sarah afterward, so she knows we're taking care of it.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: you'll talk to Tom soon, I'll talk to Sarah, and together we'll introduce fixed meeting rules. In four weeks we'll check whether anything has changed.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we can resolve the situation <g>without</g> anyone feeling put on the spot.

task.en:
A colleague is leaving the department in two weeks and has to hand over her tasks to a successor. So far, though, there's neither a complete task list nor fixed dates for the handover training, and the schedule keeps getting tighter.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Task list: Which tasks and projects absolutely need to be handed over?
Schedule: How can the handover training be organized in the remaining time?
Documentation: What should be written down?
Contact person: Who will help the successor with questions after the handover?

q.en: <r>We have a problem</r>: Ms. Meier is leaving our department in two weeks, but we still haven't really <g>brought up</g> her handover - there's neither a complete task list nor fixed dates for training her successor.

a.en: <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so there's a risk that important information gets lost if we don't act quickly now?

q1.en: Exactly, that would <g>put</g> the whole project progress <g>at risk</g>. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could sit down with her right away and create a task list with all ongoing projects and open items.

q2.en: <r>That sounds reasonable</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also set fixed training dates for the successor, so nothing gets forgotten?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. We should also clarify which documents need to <g>be available</g> before Ms. Meier leaves.

q3.en: True. And I think we should introduce new handover rules as soon as possible, so this doesn't happen again.

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>. On top of that, we could create a checklist that we use for every future handover.

q4.en: Good idea. Who should be available to the successor for questions after the official handover, in case something's still unclear?

a4.en: <r>Maybe</r> Ms. Meier could stay reachable by email as a contact person for the first two weeks, even after she's already in the new department.

q5.en: That would help. Should we talk to her about this right away, so we don't lose any more time?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could have that conversation with her today, if you prepare the checklist in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll create a complete task list, set fixed training dates, and Ms. Meier will stay reachable as a contact person for two weeks.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way the handover can go smoothly without losing any important information.

task.en:
In your team there have been frequent misunderstandings because internal emails and minutes are written very tersely and sometimes unkindly. A colleague recently complained that he felt personally attacked by an email.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Cause: What might be causing the emails to come across this way?
Wording: How can emails be phrased more positively and objectively?
Minutes: What should be kept in mind when writing minutes?
Next steps: How can you discuss this with the team?

q.en: <r>I think that</r> we should talk about a problem: a colleague recently complained that he felt personally attacked by an internal email, because it was phrased very tersely and unkindly.

a.en: I can understand that. <r>Do you mean that</r> we generally write too bluntly and not very kindly when things get stressful?

q1.en: Exactly. <r>What do you think if</r> we work out some phrasing tips together for more positive emails?

a1.en: <r>I see it exactly the same way</r>. <r>I suggest that</r> we first collect a few typical sentences that often come across as misleading.

q2.en: Good idea. <r>I have a suggestion too</r>: we could replace negative phrases like 'That's wrong' with something more neutral, for example 'Could we check that again?'.

a2.en: <r>I think that's right, though we should also keep in mind that</r> minutes are a bit different - there it needs to stay factual and concise above all.

q3.en: True, but even minutes can sound friendly without becoming imprecise. <r>I think it would be better if</r> we phrase results neutrally, but not coldly.

a3.en: <r>I completely agree with you</r>. Maybe we could create a small template that everyone can use as a guide.

q4.en: Good idea. Should we present that directly at the next meeting, so everyone knows about it?

a4.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could have the template ready by then, if you collect a few example sentences in the meantime.

q5.en: Sure. Then we can bring the topic up right at the start of the next meeting, before it gets forgotten again.

a5.en: Agreed. I think that way we'll avoid similar misunderstandings in the team in the future.

q6.en: <r>Then we can note down</r>: you'll prepare the template, I'll collect example sentences, and we'll present both at the next meeting.

a6.en: Exactly. I'm convinced our communication will be noticeably friendlier and clearer because of it.

task.en:
The 'About us' page on the company website hasn't been updated in years. It contains outdated figures and mentions neither the new locations nor the company's current products.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Content: Which information absolutely needs to be updated?
Responsibility: Who should write the new text?
Style: How should the text be phrased so it comes across as professional?
Timeline: By when should the new page be online?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: I've noticed that our 'About us' page hasn't <g>been updated</g> in years. It's missing our new locations and current products.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so the text needs to be completely revised?

q1.en: Exactly. <r>What could we do in this situation</r> to bring the page up to date again?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we can update the outdated figures fairly quickly, we just need the new revenue numbers from accounting for that.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also add a photo of our new location?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. The whole section about our products also <g>needs to be reviewed</g> again, since we've been offering the new series since last year.

q3.en: True. Who should actually write the text in the end - maybe someone from marketing?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>. Marketing knows best how to phrase things professionally, and the text will surely get proofread there too.

q4.en: Good. And by when should we realistically get this done? I don't want it to drag on for months again.

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could agree</r> on four weeks. A good text can definitely <g>be written</g> in that time without putting anyone under pressure.

q5.en: Agreed. Should we inform the marketing team this week, so they can start in time?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I'll send them a short overview today with everything that needs to be updated.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll gather the new figures and photos, the marketing team will write the new text, and the updated page should be online in four weeks.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way our company will finally have an up-to-date image again.

task.en:
There's a lot of demand at your trade fair booth, but you're short-staffed and the brochures are almost all gone. Because of this, some visitors have to wait a long time or leave unsatisfied.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Staff: How can you quickly organize more support at the booth?
Materials: How do you deal with the missing brochures?
Priority: Which visitors should be advised first?
Follow-up: How do you make sure no one gets forgotten?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: there's a lot going on at the booth right now, but there are only two of us, and the brochures are almost all gone.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so we're currently not managing to properly advise all the visitors?

q1.en: Exactly, some have already had to wait a while. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could quickly call the neighboring booth to see if someone from their team can spontaneously help out.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also offer the brochures digitally, for example via QR code?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. Then visitors can download the materials themselves, even if we don't have any left right now.

q3.en: Good idea. And how do we handle the waiting visitors? Should we take care of the ones showing concrete interest first?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>. Anyone just briefly stopping by can look at the new products first, while we take care of the serious inquiries.

q4.en: True. And what do we do if we still miss someone and they leave <g>without</g> being advised?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> keep a short list where we write down names and contact details, so we can follow up with everyone personally afterward.

q5.en: Good point. Should we do that right away, so this doesn't happen to us again?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I'll set up the list right now, while you ask the neighboring booth for support.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll get short-term support, also offer the brochures digitally, and keep a list for visitors we couldn't advise right away.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we can still handle the rest of the trade fair day well.

task.en:
Several colleagues from your department have missed their connecting train on business trips in recent months, because the announcements at the station were too late or unclear. As a result, they were repeatedly late for important client meetings.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Cause: What might be causing the connections to be missed so often?
Planning: How can trip planning be improved?
Information: How can travelers get better informed about delays?
Notification: What should happen if someone is still running late?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: over the last few months, several colleagues have missed their connecting train, because the announcements at the station were too late or unclear.

a.en: I've heard about that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so it's mainly about the poor information at the station itself?

q1.en: Exactly, and because of that some were repeatedly late for important client meetings. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: <g>everyone</g> going on a business trip could set up a train app with real-time information beforehand, then <g>no one</g> misses an important announcement anymore.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also plan more buffer time between connections, so there's still some time left even with small delays?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. <g>Some</g> connections are simply planned too tightly, a small delay is already enough and you miss everything.

q3.en: True. And what do we do if someone still ends up being late for a client meeting?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>: that person should immediately let the office know, so someone else can inform the client in time.

q4.en: Good idea. Should we write that directly into our travel guidelines, so everyone knows about it?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> present that at the next team meeting, then everyone really knows about it, and no one can say they knew nothing about it.

q5.en: Good point. Should we write down the new rules this week?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could prepare a short draft, if you look up a few good apps for train connections in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: everyone will use a real-time app going forward, we'll plan more buffer time, and whoever's still running late will contact the office right away.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way hopefully no one will miss an important appointment because of a missed train connection again.

task.en:
In a week you have to present the new product to important clients. The current presentation is written very technically, though, has hardly any images, and the product's advantages don't come across clearly.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Content: What needs to be improved in terms of content?
Structure: How should the presentation be structured?
Visuals: What images or graphics could help?
Practice: How can you best prepare for the talk?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: in a week we have to present the new product to important clients, but the current presentation is very technical and has hardly any images.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so the product's advantages don't really come across <g>because of that</g>?

q1.en: Exactly, right now technical details are mostly at the center of it, but not the benefit for customers. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could restructure the presentation and show the concrete benefit first, before getting into the technical details.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also add a few product photos and a short graphic, so it doesn't come across so dry?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. We could also show a short video connected to how the product is used.

q3.en: Good idea. And how should we best prepare for the actual talk?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>. Maybe we could practice in front of the team beforehand and ask for honest feedback.

q4.en: Good idea. Should we do that this week, so we have enough time for changes?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> do that the day after tomorrow, that would leave us a few days to adjust everything.

q5.en: Agreed. So who's actually going to take care of the new pictures and the video?

a5.en: I could take care of the pictures, if you revise the content of the presentation in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: I'll revise the content, you'll gather pictures and a video, and the day after tomorrow we'll practice together in front of the team.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way the presentation will be a lot more convincing for our clients.

task.en:
A colleague in your team behaves as if he alone were responsible for all decisions. He barely listens to the others and sometimes acts as though he already knows everything better. This is putting a strain on the team's collaboration.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Behavior: What might be causing the colleague to act this way?
Conversation: How can you bring up the topic without making the atmosphere worse?
Team spirit: How can the team's collaboration be strengthened again?
Follow-up: How do you check whether anything has changed?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: I've noticed that Paul has been behaving lately <g>as if</g> he alone <g>were</g> responsible for all decisions.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: he barely listens to the others in the team anymore?

q1.en: Exactly, and sometimes he acts <g>as if</g> he already <g>knew</g> everything better anyway. That's really straining the team spirit. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: maybe we should talk to him privately first, instead of bringing it up in front of the whole team right away.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we give him concrete examples, so he understands how his behavior comes across to us?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. <r>I can well understand that</r> he's probably not even aware he comes across <g>as if</g> he <g>didn't</g> take the others' opinions seriously.

q3.en: True, that could actually be unintentional. How can we strengthen the team spirit overall, regardless of Paul?

a3.en: That's an excellent question. Maybe we could introduce regular feedback rounds where everyone can briefly share their perspective.

q4.en: Good idea. And how do we check whether anything has actually changed afterward?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> bring the topic up again in the team in a few weeks and ask everyone how they feel about it.

q5.en: Good point. Should we have the conversation with Paul this week, so nothing gets more entrenched?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could take care of that, if you prepare the feedback rounds in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: you'll talk to Paul soon, I'll prepare the feedback rounds, and in four weeks we'll see whether the mood in the team has improved.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we can strengthen the team spirit again without Paul feeling put on the spot.

task.en:
Customers keep complaining that they get transferred to the wrong person several times on the phone before they can finally speak to the right contact. This costs a lot of time and causes frustration on both sides.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Cause: What might be causing calls to be transferred incorrectly so often?
Solution: How can you make sure calls reach the right person faster?
Training: What should the staff answering the phone additionally learn?
Feedback: How do you find out whether the situation has improved?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: several customers have complained that they get transferred to the wrong person multiple times on the phone before reaching the right contact.

a.en: I've heard about that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so the problem is mainly with the transfer at the beginning of the call?

q1.en: Exactly, and that costs customers a lot of time and causes frustration. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could put up a short overview at reception showing who's responsible for which topic, so calls get transferred correctly right away.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also introduce a standard question, for example 'What is this regarding, so I can transfer you correctly?'

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. That way the colleagues at reception can ask more specifically <g>instead of</g> just guessing.

q3.en: True. And what do we do if a request still ends up with the wrong person?

a3.en: That's an excellent question. That person could then politely say: <r>'I'm sorry, you've reached the wrong person, I'll transfer you right away.'</r>

q4.en: Good idea. Should we also offer that as a short training for everyone at reception?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> hold a short briefing where everyone practices typical sentences for such situations together.

q5.en: Good point. Should we organize that in the next two weeks?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could prepare the overview, if you take care of the training dates.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll create an overview, introduce a standard question, and everyone at reception will get a short training on transferring calls.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way our customers will be transferred to the right person much faster in the future.

task.en:
In your online meetings, technical problems come up almost every week: the connection drops, someone forgets to unmute, or loud background noise can be heard. This wastes a lot of time.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Technology: How can you improve the connection quality?
Behavior: What rules help with mute and noise problems?
Support: Who helps quickly when technical problems occur?
Preparation: How can everyone prepare better for the meetings?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: in our online meetings there are technical problems almost every week, for example the connection drops or someone forgets to unmute.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so time gets wasted in almost every meeting <g>because of that</g>?

q1.en: Exactly, sometimes even ten minutes at the start. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could ask everyone to be online five minutes before the start and quickly test their tech.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also introduce a fixed rule that everyone except the person speaking stays muted?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. That would also significantly reduce the background noise that often distracts us.

q3.en: True. And what do we do if someone still has technical problems, for example a bad connection?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>: that person could quickly write in the chat, and we'll summarize the key points for them at the end.

q4.en: Good idea. Should we also designate someone to contact technical support if there are bigger problems?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> take turns doing that, so it's not always the same person who has to deal with it.

q5.en: Good point. Should we present these rules right at the next meeting, so everyone knows about them?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could write a short overview, if you announce it in the calendar for everyone.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: everyone tests their tech beforehand, stays muted by default, and if there are problems, people write in the chat or take turns contacting support.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we'll lose a lot less time to technical problems in the future.

task.en:
In your team, everyone writes emails to customers a bit differently: some are very formal and stiff, others almost too casual. As a result, the company's image comes across as inconsistent to the outside.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Style: How can you find a consistent but friendly tone?
Template: What should a shared email template include?
Training: How can you introduce this in the team?
Control: How do you make sure everyone sticks to it?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: I've noticed that everyone in the team writes emails to customers a bit differently. Some are very stiff, others almost too casual.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: <g>as a result</g> our image comes across as inconsistent?

q1.en: Exactly, and that can leave an unprofessional impression on customers. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could create a small template for standard emails, <g>that includes</g>, for example, fixed phrases for the greeting and closing.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also collect a few examples for a friendly but not too casual tone while we're at it?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. The new colleagues who don't feel so confident yet could especially benefit from that.

q3.en: True. And how do we best introduce the template to the team?

a3.en: That's an excellent question. Maybe we could present it briefly at the next meeting and use it to show right away how it works in practice.

q4.en: Good idea. And how do we make sure everyone actually sticks to it in the end?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> occasionally send each other an email for a quick check before it goes out to the customer.

q5.en: Good point. Should we finish the template this week, so we can get started soon?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could write a first draft, if you look up a few good example emails in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll create a shared template, present it at the next meeting, and at first we'll send each other emails for a quick check.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way our emails will come across as much more consistent and professional in the future.

task.en:
Last week, a customer was sent an offer letter with an incorrect price: the quantity didn't match the terms, and the shipping costs were missing entirely. The customer has since noticed and is now unsettled.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Correction: What's the best way to handle the mistake with the customer?
Cause: What might be causing mistakes like this to happen?
Control: How can offers be better checked in the future?
Trust: How can you restore the customer's trust?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: last week a customer was sent an offer with an incorrect price, and the shipping costs were missing entirely.

a.en: I've heard about that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: the customer noticed the mistake herself and is now unsettled?

q1.en: Exactly, and that naturally doesn't come across as very professional. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we should send the customer a corrected offer as soon as possible and briefly apologize for the mistake.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also offer her a small discount <g>to</g> make up for the mistake?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. That would definitely show that we take the mistake seriously and don't want to lose the customer.

q3.en: True. And how do we prevent this from happening again?

a3.en: That's an excellent question. Maybe we could introduce a rule that every offer gets briefly proofread by a second person before it's sent out.

q4.en: Good idea. And should we maybe also create a small checklist for that, with price, quantity, terms, and shipping costs?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> even build that directly into our offer template, then nothing gets forgotten anymore.

q5.en: Good point. Should we implement that this week, so we feel more confident again quickly?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could create the checklist, if you take care of the corrected offer for the customer.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: you'll send the customer a corrected offer with a discount today, and I'll create a checklist for proofreading future offers.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we'll win back the customer's trust and avoid mistakes like this in the future.

task.en:
Over the last few weeks, written customer orders have repeatedly been incomplete: information about quantity, delivery date, or billing address was missing. This led to delays and extra effort to clarify things.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Cause: What might be causing orders to be incomplete so often?
Form: How can you make sure all important information is included?
Communication: What do you do if information is still missing?
Follow-up: How do you check whether the situation has improved?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: over the last few weeks several written customer orders have been incomplete, for example information about quantity or delivery date was missing.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: that leads to delays because we have to ask first?

q1.en: Exactly, and that costs us valuable time every time. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could solve the problem <g>by</g> introducing a fixed order form with required fields.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also show customers right away which information is still missing <g>by setting up</g> an automatic confirmation email?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. That way customers notice immediately if something's incomplete, and we don't have to follow up separately.

q3.en: True. And what do we do if an order still arrives incomplete?

a3.en: <r>I think that's an excellent solution</r>: then we should ask right away and politely, ideally by phone, so there aren't any long delays.

q4.en: Good idea. And how do we make sure the form actually gets used consistently in the end?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> introduce it <g>by</g> actively sending it to all customers with the next order confirmation.

q5.en: Good point. Should we finish the form this week, so we can get started soon?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could create a first draft, if you put together the most important required fields in the meantime.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll create an order form with required fields, set up an automatic confirmation email, and if information is missing, we'll call right away.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that by implementing this consistently, orders will be incomplete much less often in the future.

task.en:
Over the last few weeks, customer complaints have been piling up — customers are complaining, among other things, about late responses and little understanding in complaint handling. Some customers are even considering switching to another provider.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Response time: How can you respond to complaints faster?
Tone: How can you deal more empathetically with dissatisfied customers?
Solution: What kind of compensation can you offer?
Follow-up: How do you make sure customers stay satisfied?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: complaints have been piling up recently, and some customers say we respond too late and show little understanding.

a.en: I've heard about that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: some customers are even considering switching to another provider because of this?

q1.en: Exactly, and we obviously can't afford that. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could set a fixed response time, for example responding to every complaint within 24 hours.

q2.en: <r>That sounds good</r>. <r>What do you think if</r> we also collect a few fixed phrases for the opening lines of a response, like <r>'We're very sorry that problems have occurred'</r>?

a2.en: <r>Yes, I think that's a good idea</r>. That way every response sounds more empathetic right away, even when things get stressful.

q3.en: True. And what do we offer customers if there really is a mistake on our end?

a3.en: That's an excellent question. Maybe we could offer a discount or a voucher as compensation, for example.

q4.en: Good idea. And how do we make sure customers stay satisfied in the end?

a4.en: <r>Maybe we could</r> check in briefly again a week or two later and ask if everything's fine now.

q5.en: Good point. Should we discuss these new rules with the whole team at the next meeting?

a5.en: Yes, that would make sense. I could prepare a short overview with the phrases, if you take care of the response times.

q6.en: <r>Let's summarize</r>: we'll set a fixed response time, use empathetic phrases, offer compensation for mistakes, and follow up with customers afterward.

a6.en: Exactly, that's what we'll do. I think that way we'll win back the customers' trust and lose fewer customers to complaints in the future.

task.en:
In your department, there have recently been several requests from colleagues who want to return from parental leave working part-time or with more flexible hours. So far, though, there are no consistent rules for handling such requests.

Discuss with your conversation partner how you would respond appropriately to this situation.

These points can help you.
Criteria: What should determine who gets part-time or flexible hours?
Communication: How do you inform employees about their options?
Fairness: How do you make sure everyone is treated fairly?
Implementation: How do you introduce new rules in the team?

q.en: <r>We should talk about a problem</r>: recently several colleagues have shown interest <g>in</g> working part-time or with more flexible hours after parental leave, but we don't have any consistent rules for that yet.

a.en: I've noticed that too. <r>Did I understand you correctly</r>: so far we're deciding that more on a case-by-case basis?

q1.en: Exactly, and that can quickly come across as unfair. <r>What could we do in this situation</r>?

a1.en: <r>I have an idea</r>: we could set clear criteria for what determines entitlement to part-time work, for example depending <g>on</g> the position and tasks.
