<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering whether sales staff should be allowed to decide on discounts in offer letters themselves in future. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> it makes no sense to consult management specifically for every small discount, because this often costs us valuable time during the sales conversation.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we could react much faster to individual customer requests, for example regarding special prices, cash discounts or payment terms, instead of waiting for approval for days.

<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that some colleagues from the finance department told me that too much freedom with terms and conditions would be risky for our calculations and profit margin.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> we combine both approaches by setting clear upper and lower limits for discounts and delivery terms, within which sales staff can then decide independently.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
David

topic.en: Stricter rules for cancellations and returns

task.en: Management is considering tightening the rules for cancellations and returns, because too many orders are cancelled at short notice or sent back without a valid reason. Until now, customers could cancel orders free of charge right up until shortly before delivery.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,
<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering tightening the rules for cancellations and returns. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.

<r>I am of the opinion that</r> we solve the problem best by stating a clear, short deadline for free cancellations already in the order confirmation, because until now some customers have simply taken too much advantage of this option.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> this avoids many unnecessary costs, because fewer orders are cancelled shortly before the delivery date and we save on storage space and shipping costs.

<r>On the other hand</r>, it is not always easy for customers to judge whether an order really suits them before it has even arrived, and overly strict rules could put some people off buying altogether.

<r>That is why I propose that</r> in the case of legitimate return reasons such as a defect, refunds or exchanges remain uncomplicated, while we only charge a small fee for unjustified, last-minute cancellations in future.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Anna

topic.en: Standardized complaint management with a fixed response time

task.en: Management wants to introduce standardized complaint management, in which every complaint must be processed within 48 hours and an initial response given to the customer. Until now, complaints have been handled at different speeds, which has led to customer dissatisfaction.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to introduce standardized complaint management with a fixed response time, because complaints have been handled at different speeds until now. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> this innovation really makes sense. It is precisely with complaints that it becomes clear how professional and accommodating we really are as a company.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we could give customers at least an initial response within 48 hours, in order to prevent customer dissatisfaction from the outset.

<r>On the other hand</r>, several colleagues from customer service have told me that a fixed 48-hour deadline is sometimes hardly achievable for complicated complaints, especially when proof still needs to be checked.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> at least an initial confirmation of receipt can be guaranteed within the deadline, even if the actual resolution of the case takes a bit longer.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Alex

topic.en: More flexibility for parents after parental leave

task.en: Management is considering automatically granting parents the right to part-time work with flexible hours after parental leave, in order to better balance work and family. Until now, every part-time arrangement had to be applied for and approved individually.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering automatically granting parents the right to part-time work after parental leave, so that parental allowance, childcare and work can be balanced better overall. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.

<r>I am of the opinion that</r> every parent should automatically be entitled to a part-time position after parental leave, because until now every arrangement had to be applied for individually and often laboriously.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> this significantly improves the compatibility of work and family, by automatically enabling part-time work after parental leave instead of examining each individual case separately.

<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that the more employees go part-time at the same time, the more difficult staff planning becomes, especially when there is a shortage of coverage in the team.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> we take into consideration both the needs of parents and operational workflows, for example with a fixed lead time for applications.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Mark

topic.en: Termination agreements instead of dismissals in staff reductions

task.en: Management is considering relying more on mutually agreed termination contracts with severance pay instead of ordinary dismissals for upcoming staff reductions. Until now, dismissals have mostly been issued without prior consultation with the works council.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering relying more on mutually agreed termination contracts with severance pay instead of ordinary dismissals for the upcoming staff reductions. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> in such situations we should try to find mutually agreed solutions together, instead of hastily issuing an ordinary dismissal.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> a fair termination agreement with severance pay ensures that those affected still remain entitled to unemployment benefits, without having to fear a subsequent waiting period.

<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider: whoever agrees to a severance payment often also waives the right to take legal action before the labor court, in case the dismissal would actually have been invalid.

<r>That is why I propose that</r> there be a mandatory consultation with the works council before every final decision, so that the interests of everyone involved are taken into account from the outset.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Julia

topic.en: Mandatory employee review with goal agreement

task.en: Management wants to introduce a mandatory annual employee review with a fixed goal agreement for all staff, in order to make career planning and development opportunities more visible. Until now, such conversations only took place irregularly and without a standardized structure.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to introduce a mandatory annual employee review with a fixed goal agreement for all staff, in order to make career planning and development opportunities more visible. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> this innovation is really overdue, because several colleagues have told me that the previous feedback was rather random and poorly structured.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> a fixed employee review helps to specifically develop each individual's potential and no longer leave career planning to chance.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that no conversation should become a mere obligatory exercise with pre-filled forms, otherwise the goal agreement quickly loses its actual purpose.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> in these conversations we discuss both professional development and personal career planning together, so that real development opportunities become visible.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Nina

topic.en: Digital tool for self-service shift swapping

task.en: Management is considering introducing a digital tool that allows employees to independently swap shifts in the schedule and organize cover, without having to involve the shift supervisor every time. Until now, every shift swap had to be approved individually.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering introducing a digital tool for shift swaps in the schedule, with which cover can be organized independently in future. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> many problems in shift work can be solved by allowing us to swap shifts more flexibly and independently in future, instead of waiting for approval every time.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we could compensate for short-notice absences much more quickly, in order to avoid additional overtime for individual colleagues.

<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that the more freedom we have with swapping, the more confusing the entire schedule could ultimately become, if no one keeps a proper overview anymore.
<r>That is why I propose</r>: whoever wants to take on a shift should confirm this directly in the tool, while the shift supervisor still retains an overview of all changes.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
David

topic.en: Mandatory short presentation about one's own strengths

task.en: Management wants every employee to give a short presentation about their own strengths and professional values in front of the team once a year in future. Until now, there has been no opportunity to present oneself in this way.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management wants each of us to give a short presentation about our own strengths and professional values once a year in future. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.

<r>I am of the opinion that</r> such a short presentation seems unfamiliar at first. Nevertheless, I think it's a really good idea, because from my point of view, our strengths often get far too little attention in everyday work.
<r>A very important argument in favor is</r>, after all, that otherwise we can hardly make qualities like reliability or assertiveness visible, even though they are crucial for our work.

<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that, on one hand, not everyone enjoys presenting in front of the whole group, but on the other hand, this could be exactly where an important exercise for one's own presentation skills lies.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> we place special value on making the presentation voluntary and without evaluation, so that no one feels pressured.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Anna

topic.en: Communication training for clearer, more direct language

task.en: Management wants to introduce communication training to help formulate messages more clearly and directly, instead of beating around the bush for a long time. Until now, misunderstandings have occurred more often in everyday work because concerns were expressed too indirectly.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to introduce communication training to help us formulate messages more clearly and directly. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.

<r>I am of the opinion that</r> such training really makes sense, because misunderstandings, as we know, often arise exactly when we express a concern too indirectly instead of simply addressing it directly.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we have all, after all, experienced how an unclear message ultimately led to real problems in the team, even though nobody really wanted that.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that overly direct language can, after all, sometimes come across as hurtful when the right undertone or the right nuance is missing.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> in the training we also feel free to practice difficult situations in which we have to state a concern politely but still clearly and to the point.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Alex

topic.en: Written agreement and follow-up after the performance review

task.en: Management is considering introducing a binding written agreement with concrete goals and a fixed follow-up date after every performance review. Until now, many verbal agreements from the annual review, such as those about salary adjustments, have often had no consequences.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is considering introducing a binding written agreement with a fixed follow-up date after every performance review. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> we should really change this, because at the moment it often seems as if the goals agreed on in the annual review are simply forgotten after the meeting.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> writing down the agreement in writing ensures much more commitment, especially when it comes to topics such as salary adjustments or specific development opportunities.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that not every goal is already fully thought through at the time of the conversation, and some arrangements can still change in everyday work.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> there be a fixed follow-up date after every performance review, at which we check together which measures have already been implemented.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Mark

topic.en: Artificial intelligence and automation in everyday work

task.en: Management is planning to rely more heavily on artificial intelligence and automated workflows to speed up recurring tasks. Until now, such tools have only been used sporadically and without uniform data protection rules.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to rely more heavily on artificial intelligence and automated workflows to speed up recurring tasks in our digital work. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> increasing automation can really relieve us in the long run, because many recurring tasks currently cost us an unnecessary amount of time.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we could focus more on more demanding tasks by delegating simple, repetitive processes to AI-supported tools.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that no system is completely error-free, and especially when it comes to data protection and cybersecurity, we cannot afford to compromise.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> before introducing any new tool, we pay attention to both GDPR compliance and solid data encryption.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Julia

topic.en: English as the new corporate language

task.en: Management is planning to introduce English as the official corporate language, in order to facilitate international cooperation with our new trading partner. Until now, internal communication has been almost exclusively in German.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to introduce English as the official corporate language, in order to facilitate international cooperation with our new trading partner. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r>, given our increasingly internationally oriented cooperation with our trading partners, this change really makes sense.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> with a common language we can avoid intercultural misunderstandings during business trips and in contact with our new subsidiary abroad, in order to save time and nerves.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider: whoever has hardly spoken English until now needs time and support to really feel confident in everyday work.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> we offer free language courses to all employees, because the earlier we start, the easier the transition will be for us later.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Nina

topic.en: Binding code of conduct for sustainability and ethics

task.en: Management is planning to introduce a company-wide code of conduct that bindingly regulates topics such as sustainability, diversity and anti-corruption, in order to meet new statutory reporting obligations. Until now, there have only been non-binding recommendations on these topics.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to introduce a company-wide code of conduct for sustainability and ethics, in order to meet the new statutory reporting obligations. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.

<r>I am of the opinion that</r>, given our growing environmental responsibility and the new reporting obligation, we should not wait any longer, because until now there have only been non-binding recommendations on these topics.

<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> reducing our carbon footprint through renewable energy and greater energy efficiency also saves real money in the long run, instead of just causing additional costs.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that no code of conduct alone solves the problem if topics such as compliance and corporate ethics are not really lived out in everyday practice.

<r>That is why I propose that</r> we pay equal attention to both diversity and equal opportunity as well as anti-corruption and a functioning whistleblowing system, so that the code is more than just a piece of paper.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
David

topic.en: Fixed training budget for future skills

task.en: Management is planning to provide all employees with an annual training budget for topics such as agile working, digital transformation and future skills. Until now, there have been no fixed funds for this, and training courses usually had to be justified individually.

parts.en: Dear colleagues,

<r>as you probably already know</r>, management is planning to provide all employees with an annual training budget for topics such as agile working and digital transformation. <r>I would also like to write something on this topic in our blog today</r>.
<r>I am of the opinion that</r> this idea is really overdue, because the more we invest in our own future skills, the better prepared we are for changes in everyday work in the long run.
<r>A very important argument in favor is that</r> we can develop our skills in a targeted way, in order to really keep pace with digital transformation and new methods such as Scrum or Kanban.
<r>On the other hand</r>, one should also consider that in the stressful everyday work routine it is often not so easy to find any time for training courses at all, even if a budget is available.
<r>That is why I propose that</r> we block fixed learning times directly in the calendar, for example by reserving a short period each week specifically for training.
<r>What do you think about this? I'm curious to hear your opinion.</r>
Anna

topic.en: Wrong sinks delivered

betreff.en: FW: Complaint: Defective goods

mail_boss.en:
Hi,

could you please take care of the attached email? Ms Wenger from Bade-Traum ordered our bathroom products for the first time and immediately reported this problem. That's obviously not good. Please write to Ms Wenger and politely explain how the problems could have happened. We can of course also offer some form of compensation so we don't lose her as a customer.

Thanks and best regards,
Tim Holzmann
Team Leader

betreff.en: Complaint: Defective goods

mail_client.en:
Dear Mr Holzmann,

your delivery arrived two days ago: two sinks each in three colours. Unfortunately, I had to notice that the sinks are different models than what was ordered. I expect the goods I ordered. Since my customers are very demanding, the delivered products are unfortunately not acceptable. There were even already two reservations for the models I had expected. I now have to keep these customers waiting, which reflects badly on me. Please collect the wrong sinks as soon as possible and deliver the correct ones to me. At your prices, I expect better service. Whether I continue to order from you also depends on a suitable offer on your part.

Best regards,
Jutta Wenger

options.en: the sinks are of poor quality.
her customers were not satisfied.
she received the wrong goods.
expects a replacement for the sinks.
no longer wants to order from the company.
wants to pay less for the delivery.

parts.en: Dear Ms Wenger,
<r>thank you very much for your message.</r>
<r>First of all, we would like to apologise to you for the fact that</r> there was a faulty delivery of the sinks you ordered.

<r>Unfortunately, there was a mix-up with the orders.</r> During packing, the sinks were accidentally swapped. <r>We assure you that this mistake will not happen again.</r> We will deliver the correct sinks to you today and collect the wrongly delivered goods from you at the same time.

As compensation, we can offer you a discount of €50 per sink as well as free delivery on your next order.
We hope that you are satisfied with this solution and thank you for your understanding.

Julia Neumann
Customer Service

topic.en: Defective batteries in e-scooters

Thanks and regards,
Kenji Sato
Head of Sales

betreff.en: Complaint E-scooters Reg. No. 2P787-03, -04, -07, -09

mail_client.en:
Dear Ms Haruna,

as just discussed on the phone, please find below our written complaint regarding the above-mentioned e-scooters. After we had accepted a delivery delay of six weeks, we now had to find out that the batteries are defective in four of the ten scooters. According to your information, the batteries cannot be replaced, and at short notice only replacement scooters without our company logo are available. Since the scooters are used for advertising purposes, they have no added value for us without the logo. This means we would have to wait a further two to three weeks for delivery. We can only agree to this if you grant us a discount of €100 for each defective scooter, plus a one-off €100 for the further delay in delivery. Originally, a price of €5,000 for ten scooters was agreed. We assume that you will accept a final price of €4,500.

Best regards,
Matthias Schrödinger
Head of Field Sales

options.en: the delivery was delayed again.
some of the scooters' batteries are defective.
the scooters don't have a company logo.
a complete replacement of all ten scooters.
immediate delivery of the replacement scooters with the logo.
a discount for the defective scooters.

parts.en: Dear Mr Schrödinger,
<r>thank you very much for your email, in which you</r> described the problems with the e-scooter batteries.

<r>We very much regret that</r> there have been problems with the e-scooter batteries. <r>We are also very sorry that</r> we cannot immediately provide you with replacement scooters bearing your company logo.
<r>We have since found out that</r> isolated errors actually occurred during the production of the batteries.

We understand very well that under these circumstances you would like a discount. Unfortunately, we cannot grant it in the amount requested, since you already received a ten percent volume discount on the order. However, it is possible to reduce the price per defective scooter by €50, so that we will invoice you a total of €4,750 for the e-scooters. In addition, we offer to extend the warranty by a further year to three years.
We hope you agree with this solution, and remain.
Best regards,
Nina Haruna

topic.en: Incorrect invoice amount – missing volume discount

Please clarify this quickly and offer him a small credit note as compensation so the business relationship doesn't suffer.

Thanks and regards,
Sabine Bergmann
Accounting Team Leader

betreff.en: Complaint regarding invoice no. 2026-0847

while checking your invoice no. 2026-0847 for our last order, I noticed that the agreed eight percent volume discount was not deducted. I ask for prompt processing and a corrected invoice with the correct net and gross amounts. Until this is clarified, I unfortunately feel compelled to withhold payment. I expect a swift solution, within a week at the latest, otherwise we will have to reconsider our further orders with you.

Weber Elektrotechnik GmbH

<r>Unfortunately, a mistake was made on our part, for which we would like to apologise.</r> We are very sorry that this caused you additional effort.

<r>We have since found out that</r> errors occurred during the switch to our new billing software. In the process, neither was the agreed volume discount applied correctly, nor was VAT calculated on the correct net amount.

David Berger

topic.en: Delayed delivery of restaurant equipment

betreff.en: Complaint about delayed delivery – please take care of it

The opening is coming up soon, so this is obviously particularly annoying. Please apologise to her, explain the delay and offer her a voucher as well as express delivery.

Thanks and regards,
Markus Weiler
Logistics Team Leader

topic.en: Poor customer service – no response despite multiple inquiries

betreff.en: Customer service complaint – please take care of this personally

Please apologise to him, explain how this could have happened, and offer him suitable compensation.

Thanks and regards,
Petra Sommer
Head of Service

betreff.en: Complaint: No response despite multiple calls

Should the situation not improve, I will unfortunately be forced to cancel our support contract.

Best regards,
Tobias Reinert
IT Manager

options.en: the ordered software is faulty.
despite several calls, he received no response.
he paid too much for support.
may possibly cancel the support contract.
demands a full refund.
asks for a replacement device.
